4- It can also be said that they are the seven sacraments of the Church which God offered us in His holy book. This new scene in heaven which John saw is the presence of a great book, that is, at the right hand of God on His throne, and sealed with seven seals.

A strong angel: that is, strong in his voice to convey his message to all the inhabitants of heaven and earth. Who is worthy...: that is, of the honor of this book, is there anyone of all God's creation who is worthy to open its seals and disclose its mysteries?!! And this exclamatory question is considered an introduction to the answer in (v. 3).
No one of God's creation was able, because all feel their unworthiness, and this feeling did not enable them to look upon the book and its seals...

Heaven... earth... under the earth: an expression St. John used to declare the inability of anyone of God's creation, visible and invisible, men or angels or demons (under the earth), to approach this book.

St. John wept while in the Spirit after he saw the inability of all to approach the book. And this weeping means his deep sorrow at his inability to know the content of this book and his despair of anyone's ability to open it, and consequently that there was no one to save man and lift from him the judgments of God and restore his happiness to him.
God's consolation came quickly to St. John, for the tender God never delays answering a petition offered with the tears of His beloved children...

One of the elders: that is, one of the twenty-four priests near the throne, and his answer came to John to reassure him, so he commanded him: first not to weep, that is, not to grieve but to rejoice; second, he presented the Person who alone can open the book and declare its true mysteries. As for the attributes which the priest (elder) declared here, they are:

a- The Lion.. of the tribe of Juda.. of course what is meant here is the Lord Christ, for in Him the prophecy of Jacob was fulfilled (Gen 49:9), and the lion is a reference to the strength of the Lord Christ, His victory and His kingship.

b- The Root of David: that is, the originator of David and his Creator (Rom 15:12), and Christ Himself called Himself by the same title in (ch. 22:16) when He said "I am the root and the offspring of David," that is, his Creator and born of his seed according to the flesh.
The summary: no one can open the book and its seven seals except its Owner, who is Christ, to whom be glory.
Christ alone is able to save you from all your sins, so hold fast to His holy name and repeat it in all your tribulations and be nourished by His Body and Blood, and the demons will fear you.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: In the midst of the throne and of the four beasts.. and in the midst of the elders.. it is the same scene explained in detail in a Lamb as it had been slain, standing: the talk here is about the Lord Christ who rose from the dead, and in the midst of the throne means His atoning mediation between God the Father and all men, while the expression as it had been slain means that although He redeemed us and rose from the dead victorious, He bears the mark of His love and His redemption of us as a living and continual sacrifice, offering Himself to us in every Divine Liturgy so that we may enjoy union with Him and abiding in Him.
Seven horns: the horn signifies strength, and seven horns means the completeness of His strength.

Seven eyes: that is, the completeness of knowledge and penetrating insight, and St. John continues his words and says the seven Spirits of God, that is, that the completeness of His knowledge is itself His Holy Spirit who searches all things (1 Cor 2:10) and who is sent from the Son (Jn 15:26) into all the earth to complete and continue the work of God in His creation for its salvation.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: So the Lamb, the sacrifice (the Son), came with all His authority and took the book out of the hand of His Father (the One who sat); and before His divinity and the power of His authority all the heavenly creation fell down in reverence to Him, as it had submitted and fallen down before the Father earlier (ch. 4:10). Harps: musical instruments used for praise in Jewish worship.
Vials: the vial is the censer set aside for burning incense.

The meaning is that the constant work of the heavenly creation before God is praise (harps) and prayer (incense), as David says, "Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense" (Ps 141:2). The prayers of saints: that is, the incense (the prayers) offered before God is not only the prayers of the heavenly creation but also the prayers of the saintly children of God, raised from all the earth, mixed with and accompanied by the prayers and intercessions of the heavenly ones before His glory, and for this reason the Church teaches us that when we conclude our prayers before God we attach to them the intercessions and petitions of the saints who always stand before God.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: As for the praise they were offering, "St. John" described it as a new song.
"New" because he had not heard the like of it before among the hymns they were accustomed to pray with.

"New" because its subject was the redemption of Christ offered on the Cross and meditation on His being slain for us. "New" because the feeling of praise, although its words are repeated, is new in its feelings and taste, as though we praise every day for the first time.

"Hast redeemed us": the redemption that Christ offered was for men only, for Christ was not crucified to redeem the angelic heavenly creation; but their praising with the word "redeemed us" means that they pray and praise on behalf of the tongue of all who accepted the redemption of Christ, and this confirms the faith of the Orthodox Church in the connection of the Church of heaven with her spiritual creatures to the striving Church of God on earth, and for this reason, as we said before, we ask for their intercession and their prayers for us.
Out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation: that is, the redemption was offered in Christ to all peoples of every race and is no longer limited to one specific people.

The twenty-four priests declared their joy in Christ the Redeemer, so they sang a new song in which they declared their faith in His salvation offered to all mankind, which He accomplished on the Cross, and gave everyone who believes in Him a new life in Him.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: See the explanation of (ch. 1:6).

Besides the previous interpretation of the same verse in the first chapter, it can also be said that the heavenly creation, while praising Christ its Redeemer, with our tongues also, offers Him thanks for His grace overflowing upon us, since we have become united with Him in His mystical Body (He made of us spiritual kings after His image and likeness), and just as the earth is under the feet of its king, so also it has become under our feet with all its enticements, and the death of Christ made the priests of the New Testament not offer animal sacrifices like the priests of the Old Testament but the loftiest sacrifice, which is the sacrifice of the Body and Blood of Christ which He offered on the Cross, and which they offer every day on the altar of the New Testament.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: Continuing the description of the same heavenly scene, "St. John" adds that he also saw, beyond what came before, numbers of angels that cannot be counted, which he expressed as ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands. Thousands of thousands: the million or the billion was not known in counting or numbering anciently, and for this reason the expression thousands of thousands does not mean a few thousands but means thousands upon thousands, that is, the angels were numbered in the millions. And this accords of course with the expression "ten thousand times ten thousand," and the myriad is ten thousand, and what is meant is the large and vast numbers of angels who sing around the throne.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: As for the subject of the praise, it was offering glorification, thanks and acknowledgment to the Lord Christ (the slain Lamb) for the sake of His redemption of us, and this hymn included 7 attributes to indicate the completeness of the attributes of the Master.

Worthy... to receive: that is, You are worthy that these attributes be ascribed to You because they are from You and You are their source. And the attributes with which Christ was described all relate to His divinity and His equality with the Father, since these attributes are also what was uttered in the hymn offered to the Father (see ch. 4:11). In summary, you, O slain Lamb (Christ the Redeemer), are: (1) The God Almighty, so we fear nothing while You are with us.
(2) Rich in Your grace, which we touch every day in our lives.
(3) You are the fullness of wisdom, for You are the Word of the Father.
(4) Yours is the strength, for by His strength He saves us from all our sins.
(5) Yours is the glory, for it is complete in His divine greatness.

(6) Honor and blessing, for He is the source of every blessing in the world and His children enjoy it in all their circumstances, and He is honored in the eyes of all the heavenly and the earthly, and nothing has honor except through Him.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: This verse came as an affirmation and continuation of the previous one, but it brought out two new things:

Every creature which is in heaven and on the earth: that is, the praise was not limited to the heavenly creation but the earthly children of God also took part in it, as well as all beings (such as the fishes) and the invisible creation (under the earth). The second addition is the affirmation of the equality of the Father with the Son, since the Father and the Son (the One who sits and the Lamb) share, in the same measure, in the same words of glorification offered by all creation.

entries.section: (2) Second: the hymn of the Lamb

paragraphs.text: Amen: truly, in truth.

And when the hymn was offered by all the heavenly and earthly creation, those who represent it before the throne (the four beasts) answered, acknowledging and affirming all that was in it, and declaring that by their confirming reply "Amen," while the twenty-four priests did not speak but expressed the awe, honor and glory of the Lamb and of the One who sits on the throne by their prostrating and pouring themselves out before the two of them, with all the contrition and reverence that befits this awesome and wonderful scene of the Lord God.

Oh, my soul.. all creatures.. even the fishes and the mountains, indeed every breath praises the name of the Lord and glorifies Him.. so where are you in all this.. and how do you deprive yourself of sharing with the heavenly ones in praising the name of the holy Lord... begin, even with a little, and if you do not know how, why do you not strive at least by going to the church to praise and glorify the name of God?... and we now live in plenty and all the means have become available... I beseech you, my soul, not to lag behind from the beauty of this heavenly scene... for whoever praises on earth becomes numbered with the angels of heaven. Come, rise up, and do something.

The opening of the first six seals, a general introduction to the seals: the seals signify something hidden from men, and loosing them means that God wanted to declare to us what was hidden from us, and the seals all point to events that will happen in the earthly world from the ascension of Christ into heaven until His coming, and the first four seals are concerned with these.. while the other three are scenes of heavenly matters that God also teaches us about.

The Lamb opened: that is, Christ alone has the right to declare what He wants to declare to His creation, and the phrase opened a seal also indicates that He discloses to us a trick or a problem that may hinder a person from reaching God.

I heard one: the first of the angelic creatures (of the four beasts) called to John with a loud voice, as it were the noise of thunder, a voice that accords with his form (like a lion), and this strong voice was a warning of the importance of what John was about to see.

A white horse: the white horse points to victory, since the Roman commanders were accustomed to ride decorated white horses when they returned triumphant, and here the horse represents the Church with her pure apostles and her saints, for since she carries her Christ (the one sitting on it), victory has become assured to her in Him and by Him.

He that sat on him: He is Christ Himself, the secret of the Church's strength and victory; "a bow was given unto him," that is, He fights her wars and gains the victory for her (Ex 14:14), and "a crown was given unto him" because He is her only King and the Controller of all her affairs. Conquering, and to conquer: that is, victory is an essential attribute in Him and not something added to Him, and it also means that He is not like anyone else who may conquer at one time and be conquered at another.

Since the seals following this seal carried kinds of suffering and striving against evil, and woes about to come, God wanted to reassure His loving children who hold fast to their faith, so the opening of the first seal came encouraging, speaking of the victory and its completion and the assured triumph of the Church by her Christ, her leader... and these words are for all of us.

If the wars or the sufferings of the Church grow severe, we must not faint or be shaken or let our confidence in Christ weaken; we only need to remember these words "conquering, and to conquer," and hope returns and confidence returns to us. Note: some may ask how the Lamb who opened the book can be Christ and also the One who sits on the throne be Christ... and here we return to the saying that all these scenes are spiritual, heavenly and symbolic, and the proof of that is that the Lord Christ declares Himself in the Book of Revelation in more than one form and with more than one attribute and appearance.
The second angel (like a calf, ch. 4:7) called out like what the first called out, summoning St. John to look and contemplate.

After the scene of the first horse came reassuring.. the scene of the second horse came disturbing, for its color is red, that is, bloody, and the one sitting on it is the authority of evil and he has great power (a great sword). He will stir up persecutions against the Church, and also many wars in all generations until people long for peace and no one finds it except the one who has put his hope and confidence in Christ.. and this horse and its rider agree with all that the Lord Christ said and foretold in His discourse recorded in (Mt 24); it represents the different ages of persecution in which a great number of Christians are martyred.
"Was given": it indicates that although wars are the doing of men and the thought of Satan, they are by God's permission, and perhaps He intended by them discipline, repentance and return.

The martyrs have a great standing in the Church because they offered their whole lives for the sake of Christ. So try to bear the tribulations you pass through and give up some of your desires for the sake of love and peace, and so win souls for Christ.

The scene of calling to St. John is repeated, and the one who calls here is the third being, whose face was as a man (ch. 4:7). A black horse: it points to death because of the famines coming upon the world.

A pair of balances in his hand: the balance signifies hunger.., for instead of using the measure, which signifies abundance of grain, he uses the balance, which signifies scarcity and the dividing of food by weight, and this accords with what Ezekiel also prophesied, "Behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight" (Ezek 4:16).
A further clarification and description of the picture of the hunger and famines to come.

"A measure of wheat": that is, the price of a quantity of wheat (a Greek unit), which is the least possible amount on which a person can live on bread in one day, and the penny is the wage of a whole day (Mt 20:9), and the meaning is that a person's wage for a day will not be enough for him for one day's bread.

"Three measures of barley": barley is the food of the poor and a bread worse than wheat bread is made from it.. and the meaning is that even barley bread will not be available but a person will get it with difficulty. And see thou hurt not the oil and the wine: despite the famine and hunger about to come upon the world and the authority of this horseman, he will not be able to take away from the Church her joy (her wine) or the work of the Holy Spirit (her oil). The spiritual meaning in all this is that besides the real famines that come upon the world from time to time, there is also death and perdition (a black horse) as a result of man's hunger for the word of God and his poverty of it, but God always keeps His mercies for the one who takes refuge in Him by the work of His Holy Spirit within him and his constant satisfaction with His most holy Blood, which is symbolized (by the wine).

Before difficult times come in which the word of God is scarce, such as your being busy with many things, or your being struck with illnesses, or persecutions arising, seize the opportunity now and care about reading the Holy Bible and attending the spiritual meetings, and enjoy partaking of the Holy Mysteries.
At the opening of the fourth seal the fourth beast (like an eagle) (ch. 4:7) called out like those before him, "Come and see," and what St. John saw was:

A pale horse: in the English translation and others it is called the Pale-hourse, and it is a reference to a heresy and a heterodoxy brought forth by the person of an impostor, and because of his seriousness he is called "Death," and Death is not only a name for him but also the end of whoever follows him and follows his faith.

Hell followed with him: hell (Hades) means the abode of the dead, and it also signifies the place of the forces of evil; and the meaning is that the destiny of whoever accepts this teaching, strange to the faith, is death and perdition; and the author of this heresy (the strange faith) will use all available means to fight the faith of the children of God, such as killing by the sword to spread his claim, or starvation and persecution.

With the beasts of the earth: that is, his followers, and the word beasts was used to indicate the harshness of their natures and the severity of their ravaging of the peoples they enter and whose goods they drain.

Power over the fourth part of the earth: that is, God's mercies did not allow the heresy of this deceiver to spread over more than a quarter of the earth, for God is the keeper of the faith of His children, and however fierce and destructive the danger, it is limited before His power.

My beloved brother... this pale horse is frightening... do you not see with me that it has swallowed many (a quarter of the earth), so be on guard and guard your house and your children against any strange faith that the Church of Christ does not teach in her sound faith, and do not forget that its name is Death and Hell follows with it.

entries.section: (5) The fifth seal and the new vision

paragraphs.text: The souls of them that were slain: everyone who accepted suffering and martyrdom for the sake of the faith and the word of truth. Under the altar: since the altar is the holiest place in the life of the Church, where the believer meets Christ the Sacrifice, the Redeemer and the Savior, so God assigned the martyrs the holiest similar place in heaven, where Christ's constant and continual presence is, that is, they are the nearest of people in standing to Him, as compensation for their sufferings, for everyone who lays down his life for God becomes the nearest of people to Him and the most enjoying of Him.

entries.section: (5) The fifth seal and the new vision

paragraphs.text: They cried with a loud voice: we understand from these words the following...
1- That the saints who are in heaven have feelings, for the crying comes as an expression of feeling.
2- That they know what happens on earth and that heaven is an extension of their life, for they have not forgotten what happened to them.

3- God permits the saints in heaven to speak with Him, and He answers them also (v. 11). For this reason our doctrine of the intercession of the saints is an expression of a scriptural faith, since they have not been separated from us but the form of their life has changed, so that they are occupied with nothing but God, speaking with Him and remembering us before Him. How long, O Lord... dost thou not judge and avenge our blood: it is not fitting to say that the souls of the saints carry with them in heaven the desire for revenge.. rather it is a communion with the divine justice that comes near to prayer... as the prophet David said, "How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD?" (Ps 13), and this communion and prayer in its meaning is a declaration from God to us that He does not forget the blood of His children, as He said to Cain, "the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me" (Gen 4:10). We can also say that these holy martyrs do not ask vengeance on particular people but vengeance on the whole kingdom of evil, and this is of course permissible spiritually.

entries.section: (5) The fifth seal and the new vision

paragraphs.text: God did not answer their request at the beginning, but rewarded them with a great heavenly reward: He first clothed them with white robes as a symbol of joy, purity and holiness, then gave them rest out of the overflow of His love.
A little season: that is, they will wait in this state of glory and rest for a little time compared with the glories of eternity.

Until their fellowservants should be fulfilled: here God's answer to their question "How long?..." came, for God teaches them that the time of the striving Church is not yet complete.. and there are still some persecutions that reach the point of martyrdom.. but when the appointed time comes and the Church completes her witness, the general resurrection comes and the judgment of the wicked and the reward of the righteous are revealed.

May we not be shaken by what the Church passes through of suffering... for this is her portion as long as she remains a witness for Christ against the world, but let us put all our confidence and hope in Christ and His promises, and know that in the plan of His wisdom there is a time to every purpose under the heaven... so let us be strengthened by patience and confidence in God's just recompense, and may God give us grace to complete the days of our sojourn in peace.

entries.section: (6) The sixth seal and the end of time

paragraphs.text: This scene carries a vision joined to the conditions of the end of the world before the second coming of the Lord, and it completes what Christ foretold in (Mt 24). A great earthquake: that is, a great, frightening shaking that suits and corresponds to the event about to take place, and it signifies the shaking of the faith of many.

The sun became black: that is, the disappearance of the sky and of all light, and thick darkness became the prevailing thing, and this increases the sadness and terror of the scene. The sun signifies Christ, that is, Christ hid His knowledge from many because of their persistence in sin.

The moon became as blood: that is, whoever seeks a little light after the disappearance of the sun will not find it. The moon also signifies the Church, as the Song of Songs describes her, "fair as the moon" (Song 6:10), and so its turning into blood means that the Church is filled with martyrs.

entries.section: (6) The sixth seal and the end of time

paragraphs.text: As figs or any other fruit fall before the violent winds, so the stars of heaven fall and all nature dissolves) ... see what the Lord said in Mt 24:29) and the stars signify leaders in the Church who fall and depart from the faith, like the heretics.

entries.section: (6) The sixth seal and the end of time

paragraphs.text: St. John continues describing the scene that is to happen; after the elements of material life and the nature we are familiar with have passed away, heaven opens like a book that was closed and rolled up, and this comparison means that what was hidden, like the writing inside the roll of the scroll, God will declare to all. Every mountain and island were moved out of their places: the direct meaning can be joined to the signs of the end of the world, for after the passing of the sun, the moon and the stars, so the mountains pass away and the islands are moved as a result of the end of gravity with the passing of the sun. But the spiritual meaning is closer here, for the mountains and islands point to the kingdoms of the world, whether lofty like mountains or many and scattered like islands, which have no stability or value before the coming of the fearful Lord, and this meaning accords more with the spiritual description in the next verse.

entries.section: (6) The sixth seal and the end of time

paragraphs.text: The kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men: they are everyone from whom people expected steadfastness before hardships and escape from them because of their strength, their abundant money and their earthly authority.
Every bondman, and every free man: that is, all the remaining classes in society, what applied to the former will apply to them.

Hid themselves in the dens: a figurative expression whose purpose is to show the intensity of fear and terror and the desire to flee and hide while this is not available; for how can a person hide or find a way after the falling of the stars and the disappearance of the sun and the moon... or how can a person hide from the face of God?!
And the meaning is that everything a person boasts of, whether leadership or rank or abundant money or mental ability, will not profit a person at all.
Remember with me, beloved, that only the humble find favour with God (Lk 1:30), so may we learn to glory in nothing but God Himself and our relation to Him (2 Cor 10:17).

entries.section: (6) The sixth seal and the end of time

paragraphs.text: From the terror of the scene and its intensity for those not prepared to meet the heavenly Bridegroom, they wish for death or final disappearance and find nothing of this, so they cry out, addressing the mountains and rocks to fall on them so that they may not face God the Father (who sits on the throne) or God the Son (the Lamb), for they have known by the Spirit that this is the day of His wrath, that is, the day of His second coming and the revealing of His just judgment upon them, and who is able to stand or defend himself on this day, He before whom "every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty" (Rom 3:19).

The rite of the Church carries many spiritual meanings in its movements.. for at the end of the Liturgy the priest carries the Body of Christ in the paten, placing it twice in two circuits that represent two comings of the Lord Christ, the first for redemption and mercy.. and the second for the just judgment, and the people cry out in both circuits "Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord," reverently and prostrating, expressing the fear of this wonderful day, the day of the second coming of Christ... Have mercy on us, Lord... and have mercy again.

The sealing of the believers, an introduction to the seventh chapter: this chapter came as an interlude between the sixth chapter, in which the six seals were opened, and the eighth chapter, which speaks of the opening of the seventh and last seal, and since the last thing that came in the sixth seal was frightening and what will also be declared in the eighth chapter is awesome, the seventh chapter came between them to reassure the children of God and to tell them of a mark that is specially theirs, and also a picture of their heavenly inheritance.

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the children of God

paragraphs.text: God allowed St. John to see another vision before the opening of the seventh seal. He looked and saw four angels at the four corners of the earth, as though the earth had become a square flat surface before him, holding the four winds of the earth. We do not know how an angel holds winds ... but John saw and knew by the Spirit and wrote what he saw. The meaning here is that everything is subject to the authority and command of God, who has entrusted His angels with carrying out His will in protecting the earth from the violent winds that may come from any direction. If these winds were released, they would uproot all the trees, the seas would overflow because of them, and fierce storms that end life on earth would grow violent.
Wind: it signifies the justice of God in punishing the wicked.

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the children of God

paragraphs.text: Another angel ascending from the east: most of the Fathers affirmed that this angel is a new appearance of Christ in the Revelation of John, for the following reasons:
(1) He comes forth from the rising of the sun, for He is "Light of Light" and He is "the light of the world."
(2) He has the seal of God with Him, for the presence of the king's seal in his hand means that he has the same authority as the king.
(3) It is He who called out and commanded the angels not to harm the earth, and this is from His authority and by His will.
There is another opinion which says that he is one of the angels, but from among the principal and highest orders of them.

Christ came forth in a radiant appearance from the rising of the sun, carrying the authority of God His Father and the seal of the Living One (the Holy Spirit), and He gave a command to the four angels who hold the four winds of the earth to remain as they were, holding the winds, so that no harm would come upon the earth or injury to anyone until all the servants of God have been sealed with the living seal, which is the anointing of the Holy Spirit granted to us in the oil of the Holy Myron, by the signing on our foreheads and our bodies.

To whom it was given to hurt: this does not mean that they have authority to do this by their own will, for the will here is God's alone and His absolute command. As for the word "given," it means that God created them with a special power to carry this out when He commands them.

From these two verses we conclude that the final plagues will not come before God distinguishes His children from the wicked, so that nothing may harm them (see the parable of the tares and the wheat in Mt 13:30).

My beloved brother ... how great is the anointing with which we were anointed in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, and by which the Holy Spirit dwelt within us, so that we became sealed for God, bearing His name as His children and moving about as living, holy temples. Yet some of us do not realize the greatness of this gift and its responsibility. Would that we all hasten to listen to St. Paul when he warns us not to quench the Spirit (1 Thess 5:19) or grieve Him (Eph 4:30). So hasten always to repentance, my friend, that you may enjoy the work of the divine Spirit within you.

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the children of God

paragraphs.text: I heard: that is, St. John did not see the believers during their sealing, but learned by hearing from one of the angels.

A hundred and forty and four thousand: the meaning and the numbers here are spiritual and symbolic. This number is the product of the 12 tribes of the Church of the Old Testament × the 12 disciples, the fathers of the Church of the New Testament × a thousand, and the number one thousand here points to heavenly perfection ... The number as a whole means that everyone of God's people of old who waited in hope for the redemption of the Son, and everyone who accepted His redemption through the proclamation of the Gospel and of the Apostles in the Church of the New Testament, has become one of those sealed before the throne of God and enjoying Him.

Every tribe ... the children of Israel: of course the word Israel here comes in its spiritual meaning, for it is not reasonable that the Jews who rejected faith in Him and did not accept it are the "sealed," they who made the infant Church taste terrors of torment and persecution ... What confirms that the speech here is spiritual is that he mentioned the word tribes, and we know that there are at present no tribes in Israel, for they no longer keep their genealogies or their tribes.

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the children of God

paragraphs.text: In these four verses St. John begins to explain and detail what he summarized in the previous verse. He makes clear that the number of a hundred and forty-four thousand is twelve thousand sealed from each of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel ... Here it is important for us to point out the following ...

(1) In the order of the tribes here, the chronological order was not observed, as Jacob did when he mentioned the names of his sons in the order of their birth (Gen 49), beginning with his firstborn Reuben.

(2) The tribe of "Dan" is not mentioned because it worshipped idols in the land it possessed (Judg 18:29-31). So everyone who departs from the worship of God by worshipping a strange worship has his name blotted out of the book of life (Deut 29:18-25). Likewise, an ancient Jewish tradition says that the Antichrist will come from the tribe of Dan). Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5:30.((3) Joseph is mentioned as a tribe instead of the tribe of Ephraim his son, because the tribe of Ephraim fell into idolatry and allied with the enemies against Judah (Isa 7:17), and the Lord rejected them from before Him (Jer 7:15). (4) Joseph did not have a tribe of his own, for in return for his faithfulness of old he received double compared with his brothers, in two full portions for his children, so that his son "Manasseh" became a tribe and his son "Ephraim" a tribe ... and now he receives a full portion before God. In this there is a spiritual meaning and teaching that reminds us of what the Lord said: "Whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance" (Mt 13:12), "You were faithful in little, I will set you over much" (Lk 19:17). (5) It is also noticeable that the tribe of Levi, which after the Law was not mentioned as an independent tribe and did not inherit a portion in the land because it was the tribe of service ..., now stands before God in return for its service, which is the noble service of the priesthood before God.

Would that we therefore learn to strive as much as we are able, so that we obtain what Joseph obtained, namely a double portion, and not be negligent and become like "Dan" or "Ephraim," who lost everything.

After this: we move on to a new vision. In the first scene St. John was looking on the earth ... but here he continues his vision in heaven, although the subject is one: the first was the sealed Church, and here it is the triumphant Church.

A great multitude: this is a joyful scene that St. John saw, for the number here cannot be counted ... and it is something that pours all hope into the heart of the Church striving on earth ... For despite the many spiritual wars, the violence of Satan and the many temptations ... there is the work of the saving grace of God, and despite the enemies who persecute the Church in order to destroy her faith, we find that those who enter heaven are beyond number, for God is her keeper and the One who overshadows her.

All nations ... tongues: God's plan of salvation is not limited to one people to the exclusion of another. God came and became incarnate for the redemption of all mankind, so everyone who accepts His redemption and holds fast to the right faith will inherit and stand before Him who sits on the throne and before the slain Lamb. There is no distinction in heaven between color, race or language. Is He not the One "who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4)? White robes: they signify purity and holiness, for none but the pure enter heaven, while holiness is acquired by a person through his nearness to God.

Palm branches: there are no material things in heaven, and so the palm branches here are a spiritual scene that points to victory and triumph, since people used to receive the processions of victorious commanders after wars with palm branches; see also (Jn 12:13). St. John saw a great multitude that he could not count, from the different peoples of the earth, in purity, joy and victory.
Take courage, beloved ... for you have a place in heaven where there is glory, so take all care that no one steals your crown from you.

And they cried: the crying with a loud voice here is the cry of joy, jubilation and praise, for they are in a state of joy beyond imagining, and how could it not be so when they are victorious and enjoy the sight of their Redeemer and Savior!?!
Salvation to our God: this is the hymn of praise and victory, for in the rapture of their everlasting joy they proclaim the secret of this happiness ... and this hymn has two meanings:

The first: victory belongs to our God, the Almighty, the Conqueror who went forth conquering (Rev 6:2). He conquered Satan, bound him and stripped him of his authority (Lk 10:18), and conquered death and trampled it (1 Cor 15:55), and released all those who were held captive in Hades and brought them out to Paradise (Eph 4:9). The second meaning: our God is the secret of our salvation, and we would not have been saved without Him, meaning that God gave them salvation and they return the credit to its owner, thanking Him for having accomplished their victory.
Him that sitteth upon the throne, and the Lamb: that is, the hymn is offered to the Father and the Son in the same measure, and this is evidence of the equality of the two hypostases.

All the heavenly creation, with all its orders (ranks), took part in the praise and the contrite, joyful worship before God, and in their praise they offered Him the seven attributes of greatness and honor, which indicate the perfection of His attributes ... All of this was explained in detail in (ch. 4:10-11), (ch. 5:12-14).

entries.section: (2) Explanation by the elder (one of the priests)

paragraphs.text: God willed for St. John, and for us also, not to be content with watching the wonderful scene but also to know some of its secrets. For this reason one of the twenty-four priests approached him with a question whose purpose was to urge St. John to knowledge. His question meant: do you know who these are who are clothed in white robes, what their secret is, and why they stand here?! And because St. John does not know all the mysteries, he answered him with courtesy and respect: "Sir, thou knowest" (v. 14). This is a humility that teaches us to turn with our questions to the priests and fathers of the Church concerning what is hard for us to understand or apply.

entries.section: (2) Explanation by the elder (one of the priests)

paragraphs.text: This heavenly priest answered St. John as follows:

These are they which came out of great tribulation: the tribulation here may be the tribulation to which every Christian is exposed in his private life, in persecution or temptation which he bears with thanksgiving, or a persecution that passes over the whole Church and reaches the point of martyrdom for the faith. The great tribulation here may also be a reference to the period of the Antichrist's presence on earth and the wars and afflictions that will accompany his presence.

The spiritual meaning is what the Lord Christ announced repeatedly, that there must be tribulation in the world (Mt 24:9), (Jn 16:3), and what St. Paul also affirmed, that suffering and tribulation are the price of the glory revealed in us before God (Rom 8:17). Have washed their robes, and made them white: "washed" and "made white" are two inseparable actions, for washing leads to whiteness. The meaning is that for these who overcame the great tribulation, the secret of their purity, holiness and victory was the blood of the Lamb. A Christian has no strength apart from the blood of Christ, for salvation, steadfastness and purity are founded on "His precious blood."

The washing and whitening remind us of two inseparable sacraments of the Church. The first is the washing from sin in the sacrament of confession, when the priest reads the absolution and casts the filth of sin off the repentant penitent, and the whitening is actually accomplished in the blood of the only-begotten Son, so that after Communion a person goes forth pure and clean, having been united with the most holy Body and Blood of Christ.

We must all not lose heart before tribulation and pain ... however much sufferings increase upon us, let us look to heaven and trust that we have a crown. For what Stephen saw of the beauty of heaven at the time of his martyrdom made him think lightly of the temporary, limited pain compared with the unlimited glory (Acts 7).

entries.section: (2) Explanation by the elder (one of the priests)

paragraphs.text: Therefore: that is, because they passed through the great tribulation and did not lose heart, and also were cleansed by the blood of the Lamb, which cleanses from all sin (1 Jn 1:7). Are they before the throne of God: this is the dearest and greatest reward, that a person should stand in the presence of God, offering praise with the heavenly beings without ceasing, for he has become part of heaven and of the heavenly creation itself. The words "in His temple" signify absolute nearness to the unlimited divine Essence, despite the multitude of numbers beyond counting (v. 9), for each one will be near to God, enjoying Him inside His temple. Note: the word temple here does not refer to a limited place, for God is not limited by place, and likewise the expression "Him that sitteth on the throne" ... the meaning here is spiritual, and the scene is presented to us as far as the human mind can grasp it.

Shall dwell among them: in the Greek language, "will overshadow them," which is a stronger expression than the meaning of constant presence before God, for it means divine embrace, encompassing and keeping of every soul that has completed its struggle and has a place before the throne and inside the temple.

My beloved brother, our standing in the Church and seeing her sanctuary and altar remind us of this wonderful heavenly scene. Indeed, the Church during the Liturgy is heaven itself, and you are called to enjoy heaven here in the Church, to stand before the divine Presence, which we shall continue, by the grace of Christ, in His eternal Kingdom. So do not let laziness or any other hindrance keep you away from what you are called to.

entries.section: (2) Explanation by the elder (one of the priests)

paragraphs.text: They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more: St. John continues to describe the state of happiness that the victors feel. The words "they shall not hunger or thirst" first mean that they are satisfied with Christ and the divine Essence, and they are in a state of constant spiritual quenching, so the sensations of the body no longer "occupy or trouble us, and nothing diminishes the splendor of the enjoyment of God.

The word "any more" leads us to another meaning, which is that these had been subjected to torture by hunger and thirst for the sake of faith and love of God, or they were hungry and thirsty for righteousness in Christ (Mt 5:6), and now the time has come for their compensation for all their suffering. For God in His justice does not forget anyone's labor, but repays him a hundredfold, and without doubt the compensation of heaven cannot be compared with any compensation on earth.

Neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat: that is, no new burden of trials will be upon them. Solomon describes trials as the burning sun (Song 1:6), and likewise there will be no new troubles, "heat"; and how could this be when God Himself overshadows them, shelters them and shepherds them (v. 15).

entries.section: (2) Explanation by the elder (one of the priests)

paragraphs.text: The previous chapter ended with its talk about "the day of the wrath of the Lamb" and His vengeance on the wicked (ch. 6:17), and here the picture is completely different with His holy children, for He shepherds them Himself and gives Himself to them, in a beautiful and eloquent picture and in a manner easy for human beings to imagine, and He presents to us some of these pictures. Shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: this verse is connected with what came in (v. 16" (They shall not thirst ..."), for the secret of their not thirsting is their being quenched by spiritual springs that never run dry or fail, since Christ alone has become their source, and this reveals to us a new secret of the mysteries of eternity ... there we drink and receive and grow ... for eternity is not a static scene but a constant spiritual movement that carries us from perfection to perfection.

And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes: this brings us back to the justice of God and His compensation for every labor and every pain His children endured during their life on earth, ... so take courage, beloved, and bear with thanksgiving everything you pass through. How beautiful is this wonderful spiritual picture, as Christ stretches out His tender hand to pat us and wipe the tears from our eyes ... It is of course well known that there are no real tears in eternity, for the bodies are spiritual and luminous, but the meaning is a beautiful one that expresses the tenderness of God, His compassion and His compensation of His children for all their sufferings.
"The seven trumpets"
"God's warnings by the first four trumpets"

Introduction to chapter eight: chapter six carried the first six seals, which foretold some of the things coming upon the earth until the end of time. After the reassuring heavenly scene that St. John saw in chapter seven, he brings us back to the seventh and last seal, which in turn carries a new group of seven, the seven trumpets, of which the first four occupy chapter eight, while the rest come in

entries.section: (1) The opening of the seventh seal and the golden censer

paragraphs.text: When the seventh seal was opened, silence reigned in all of heaven. The silence here points to readiness and anticipation for the occurrence of something new, great and awesome.
"Half an hour" is a period of time that is not measured by earthly time, but the Fathers agreed that its mention is a figure for the shortness of this quiet period.
"The seven angels" are the seven archangels, of whom the angel Raphael said in the Book of Tobit that he is one.
"Were given" means that they were charged by God to carry the trumpets and sound them to proclaim His successive warnings to mankind as a result of their lack of repentance.
The trumpet: trumpets were a familiar sight in Jewish worship and were also used by the pagan peoples. Their most important uses were:
1- Announcing the beginning of religious celebrations.
2- Preparing for war, whether in defense or attack.
3- A warning of the working of God's power, as happened when the walls of Jericho fell after the blowing of the trumpets.

entries.section: (1) The opening of the seventh seal and the golden censer

paragraphs.text: Another angel: that is, not one of the seven archangels who carry the trumpets, but one who has a mission of intercession and supplication, as we shall see.

A golden censer ... a golden altar: since this angel stood before the divine throne and in the face of God Himself, the censer and likewise the altar could only be of pure gold, as a reference to the splendor of God's glory and to the fact that everything that stands before God is not defective or flawed.

The mission of this angel is to offer much incense, that is, fervent intercessory prayers, which were accompanied also by the intercessory prayers of the heavenly saints on behalf of the believers on earth. This heavenly scene confirms the belief of our Church in the intercession of the angels and saints, offered on our behalf at all times before the throne of God. In another symbolic interpretation: some saw that this "angel" is the Lord Jesus Himself, who stood before the altar (the Cross) carrying the golden censer (His sufferings and His atoning intercession), and the Father accepted it and accepted with it also the intercessions of the saints and their petitions.

entries.section: (1) The opening of the seventh seal and the golden censer

paragraphs.text: After the angel offered the incense, he took from the fire of the altar, which represents divine justice, and cast it upon the earth, and frightening things happened, such as thunders, lightnings and earthquakes, to alert people and warn them before the proclamation of "the warning trumpets."

My beloved brother, God in His love for us and the breadth of His heart accepts on our behalf the prayers and intercessions of the angels and saints, and He is longsuffering and slow to anger, so He does not bring upon the wicked the punishment they deserve all at once, but warns and cautions repeatedly ... But we must not forget that He is also a just and awesome God ... So do not neglect your repentance or postpone it, and take for yourself an intercessor, a friend, who supports you with his prayers before the throne of grace.
Prepared themselves: that is, got ready without haste, as a reference to God's patience with mankind, that perhaps they would repent.

Hail and fire: they remind us of God's plague upon Pharaoh in (Ex 9:23), "the Lord gave hail, and fire ran along upon the ground." The use of a noun and its opposite (hail and fire) means the breadth of the punishment and its inclusion of all degrees, as when we say "right and left" and mean all places, or we say "sweet and bitter" and mean all foods. The meaning here is that whoever escapes the "hail" and bears it is harmed by the fire, and whoever is not affected by the intensity of the heat is destroyed and killed by the hail. Mingled with blood: how can fire be mingled with hail and with blood?! These are frightening expressions that the Holy Spirit used to proclaim the divine wrath upon mankind if they do not repent.

A third part: that is, despite the just wrath of God, He does not bring upon us exactly what we deserve. His wide mercy made this punishment a third, because the purpose of these warnings is the repentance of man and his return, not the final divine retribution.
The trees and all green grass: that is, the first warning is directed to the agricultural and food goods of the earth, which represent the most important needs of man for life on earth.

When a material tribulation meets you or your needs fall short in anything, do not be disturbed, but accept it with contentment and examine yourself. Perhaps God intends that you notice a fault in you that you should correct, or something lacking that you should complete. He loves you and seeks the salvation of your soul, even if He allows a limited material hardship for you.

A great mountain burning with fire: that is, a tyrannical ruler or a great state that stirs up war (the same comparison God used in speaking of the king of Babylon in (Jer 51:25)). Was cast into the sea: the sea, in its vastness and the turbulence of its waves, points to the world in upheaval. The meaning is that the second warning is a warning of a great war that sweeps over the world in all its regions, like the world wars, and the cause of it will be the pride of a great nation, like the burning mountain. The results of this war will be: the third part of the sea became blood: that is, the death resulting from the fighting and people's destroying one another includes a third of the inhabitants of the earth, or a third of all "creatures which had life," for deadly weapons take man and animal together. The third part of the ships: the destruction of a third of the ships points to the severing of ties and communication between people, on the one hand because of the horror of the war and its results, or on the other hand because each person is occupied with his own selfishness to the exclusion of others. The whole picture is very frightening, for the word "third" here means millions of people, and death may include one person from every family. War is a human creation, the result of man's evil, although God allows it, perhaps so that it may be a severe warning for his turning back from his evil.

Whatever your position or authority, do not use it for your own benefit at the expense of others, harming them so that you may profit. Rather, make peace and love as much as you can, so that you will have a treasure in heaven to rejoice in.
When the third angel sounded, he announced to us a new problem that becomes a cause of the destruction of many.

The fall of a great star: that is, a religious leadership of standing, or a spiritual leadership that used to shine with its teachings like a lamp. But when it fell, teachings foreign to the faith came upon a third of the rivers and the springs. The rivers and the springs: these are what people quench their thirst from and drink from, and the meaning is that because of the spread of a faith foreign to the right faith of the Church, thoughts (the rivers) and feelings (the springs) became completely polluted.

The name of the star is Wormwood: wormwood is an extremely bitter herb, and this name is used as a figure for the intense bitterness of teaching foreign to the faith, for it is deadly to everyone who tastes it. It can also be said how bitter it is to the heart of God that those who were once enlightened by the sound faith should perish, then deviate and fall after the one who led them astray by his fall.
A third part of the waters: as we pointed out before, the third means that many went astray, but God in His mercies and care still keeps the remainder in their sound faith.

God entrusted the deposit of the faith to His pure Apostles and His holy Church, and our Fathers kept it for us by the tradition handed down to us with their blood ... So take refuge, beloved, in the Church and her Fathers, and do not accept bitter, destructive teaching, even if it seems sweet and smooth, so long as it is foreign to your Church and your ears have not been accustomed to it before.
A third part of the sun: our sun is our Christ.
A third part of the moon: the moon is the Church, which reflects the light of her Christ and so lights the darkness of hearts.

A third part of the stars: they are the men of God and the spiritual leaders who shine in His Church like stars. A new warning and caution comes with the fourth trumpet, for with the increase of heresies and errors, a third of the sun is struck, that is, people transgress against the Lord Christ either by denying His divinity or by not confessing Him at all, through their atheism and turning away from Him.

Likewise many reject the authority of their mother the Church (the moon) and so deprive themselves of her lights, and this darkness also includes many of the clergy (the stars), so a third of them fall, their light vanishes, and they lose the splendor of their example for the believers.
The day shone not for a third part of it, and the night likewise: that is, the darkness of evil entered the day and the night, which signifies evil, and it became more evil and more dark.

"An angel flying through the midst of heaven": he is not one of the seven archangels holding the trumpets, but this scene separates the first four trumpets from the remaining three. For this reason some of the Fathers see that this angel is the Holy Spirit Himself, who warns of what is to come.
With a loud voice: a voice of majesty and awe.
Woe, woe, woe to the inhabiters of the earth: frightening words that announce that what is to come is far worse in its terrors than what has gone before ...

Save us, O God our Savior, from the hard times and keep us in Your name, for we have no other besides You whom we hope in and for whose fatherly mercies we wait ... As long as You are with us we fear no evil, for You keep us, whatever the tribulations around us.

The fifth and sixth trumpets, introduction to chapter nine: the previous chapter contained the first four warnings and ended with a strongly worded proclamation of what is coming in the following trumpets, and for this reason the next three trumpets are called the woes, because of the terrors they contain.

entries.section: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

paragraphs.text: A star fallen: either an angel sent on assignment by God to open the gates of Hades, or it is Satan himself, given the same authority by God's permission. Perhaps this is the more probable, and it agrees with the expression "fallen," for we know that Satan was one of the archangels but fell through his pride and did not abide in the love of God.
To him was given the key: that is, he came to have authority to bring out his helpers, the demons, to war against all mankind, but within the limits of God's permission.

entries.section: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

paragraphs.text: He indeed opened the pit of the abyss, and as soon as he opened it a dense smoke came out that caused people to lose right vision.
A furnace: a burning, intensely blazing oven.

Smoke: these are the doubting thoughts of Satan and the wars of atheism, which by their density made people lose sight of the Lord Christ (the Sun of righteousness), and thick darkness wrapped them, that is, the sound faith was lost.

entries.section: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

paragraphs.text: There came out locusts: of course the locusts here are the demons, and when God pictures them to us in the form of locusts, it is so that we may know:

First: their great number; for the locust is an insect whose swarms are estimated at hundreds of millions when they attack. Second: the severity of their destruction; for the locust eats everything it meets on its way and leaves the land only bare. Unto them was given power: that is, Satan has no power over mankind unless it is permitted to him by God and within the limits of the discipline that He sees fit.

As the scorpions of the earth have power: the scorpion's sting to a man is very painful and its poison penetrating, and the use of the comparison of scorpions together with locusts is only an addition to the severity of this woe that comes upon the world.

entries.section: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

paragraphs.text: It was commanded them: that is, it was commanded by God, who determines the size, measure and kind of the discipline by His absolute authority.

The grass ... any tree: the grass signifies the little ones among the believers ... and the tree those of higher stature in the faith. The general meaning is that although God allowed Satan this blow, He prevented him from approaching the believers of all their degrees, for God, in His tenderness and love for His children, protects the weak and the strong among them from the deceptions of Satan and does not allow him to influence them or to affect them.

Which have not the seal of God: this woe strikes the people who do not have the mark of the Holy Spirit on their foreheads, and they are of two kinds. The first is the one who was not baptized and so never received the mark at all, or one who was a Christian but, because of his constant refusal of repentance, quenched and grieved the Spirit, so that Satan gained authority over him.

entries.section: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

paragraphs.text: The mercy of God appears in His not allowing harm to the point of death (killing), but only for five months, which is a period of the proclamation of God's wrath on mankind, as happened in the days of the Flood (Gen 7:24), when the waters increased for five months.

As for the degree of discipline, it is very severe, which the Holy Scripture likened to us as pain resulting from the sting of a scorpion that runs through a person's veins, and he finds no remedy for his pain.

entries.section: (1) The fifth trumpet (the opening of the abyss)

paragraphs.text: Continuing the description of the severity of people's pain from the force of the divine discipline: they wish for death to escape what has come upon them, but even death they do not obtain, and their torment continues, perhaps that they may repent.

We thank You, our tender God, for You had pity on the weakness of our faith and did not leave Satan any authority over us that would destroy our faith ... but You strengthened us and gave us an opportunity for repentance. And the punishment You allowed for others is a warning to us, so that our attachment to You may increase ... for You alone are our help, our salvation and our goal.

entries.section: (2) The features of the war in this woe

paragraphs.text: Among the pictures of God's love for His children is that He reveals to them the features and attributes of the enemy warrior so that they may prepare and not be deceived by him ... These declared attributes are nine in number and carry many spiritual meanings and symbols.

1- The shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared unto battle: the horse is the strongest and swiftest of the animals used in war, and the word "prepared" means that they will use all their strength, as though they had made ready and trained to bring man down.

2- On their heads were as it were crowns like gold: that is, they have authority and standing over people like the kings who wear golden crowns, but it is counterfeit gold by which the children of God are not deceived, because it is only like gold. It may also be a reference to material wars, the love of luxury and the grandeur of living, which entice and seduce many people.

3- Their faces were as the faces of men: that is, Satan uses helpers from among human beings who have accepted his thought and become soldiers for him, promoting him and persuading others of his evils.

entries.section: (2) The features of the war in this woe

paragraphs.text: 4- They had hair as the hair of women: that is, Satan in his wars uses every means, even the soft and alluring ones (like women).
5- Their teeth were as the teeth of lions: that is, although softness is the outward appearance of Satan's wars, ferocity and devouring are his inner reality.

entries.section: (2) The features of the war in this woe

paragraphs.text: 6- They had breastplates: breastplates of iron, that is, a symbol of hardness and severity in fighting.

7- Their wings: that is, the wings of the locusts (the demons) make a terrifying and disturbing sound, like the sound of war chariots which, in their number and multitude, spread terror in people's souls.

entries.section: (2) The features of the war in this woe

paragraphs.text: 8- They had tails like unto scorpions: curved and poisonous. The tail is the end of the matter, so even if these demons have a crown like gold, a human face and soft hair, the end is the sting with poison.

9- In their tails were stings: the burning heat (hummā) is intense embers of fire, and this expression is a figure for Satan's poison, which runs through the body like grains of blazing fire, so that the deceived person who is stung by them has severe pain.
Five months: that is, a limited period that symbolizes God's wrath; see (v. 5).

entries.section: (2) The features of the war in this woe

paragraphs.text: The angel of the abyss: that is, the chief of all the demons (the devil), who directs these wars and guides his soldiers to destroy man and cause him to lose his salvation in Christ.

His name is "Abaddon" or "Apollyon": a word whose meaning is "the Destroyer." It was mentioned in the two languages known at that time because of the importance of proclaiming his name and his attribute to everyone, so that people may guard against his thoughts ... and his deception and discover his true aim of destruction.

entries.section: (2) The features of the war in this woe

paragraphs.text: One woe: this was the first of the woes, and it is what the fifth trumpet carries, while the two other woes to come are those carried by the sixth and seventh trumpets.

Take heed, my brother, that the wars of the demons mostly take the appearance of softness and pleasure at their beginning until they make you fall, but inside them are poison, pain and burning fire, then destruction. So do not accept his lusts, however alluring they are, and if you fall, rise quickly with repentance and tears, for your God loves you and rescues you from his hand.

entries.section: (3) The sixth trumpet and the second woe

paragraphs.text: The golden altar: this is the same altar before which the angel offered incense in (ch. 8:3), and from whose fire he also took and cast it from the altar upon the earth, so that there were great warnings (ch. 8:5). Four horns: that is, the four corners of the altar, for the altar had horns on its corners. This is the picture of the altar familiar among the Jews in their worship, whether in the tabernacle of meeting or in Solomon's temple afterward. When the sixth angel sounded, the voice came from the four horns at one time, as a reference to its strength and severity on the one hand, and to its universality and its reaching the whole inhabited world on the other.

entries.section: (3) The sixth trumpet and the second woe

paragraphs.text: This voice was a divine command to the sixth angel himself to release and give authority to four angels who were bound.

The four angels which are bound: some see that they are angels who had been charged by God with carrying out what is to come upon the world in this woe, and this charge was postponed until the command is given at the sixth trumpet to loose them from their bonds. Some see that they are four demons of formidable power who have been bound since the fall of man, and God will now leave them, by His permission, to come upon the earth with evils and wars in fulfillment of the second woe!! Whether they were this or that, it will not change anything in reality, since everything happens by the command and permission of God and in fulfillment of His will.

In the great river Euphrates: the river Euphrates passed through the kingdom of Babylon, which was always a symbol in the Holy Bible of the kingdom of evil, and this means that these angels who carry out the second woe bear a severe punishment.

entries.section: (3) The sixth trumpet and the second woe

paragraphs.text: For an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year: that is, everything under heaven has a time by a precise divine plan, so nothing is before or after its appointed time, even by one minute. The purpose of this verse is to bring out a part of the divine wisdom and the attribute of God as "the Controller of all."

The third part of men: punishment by a third was constantly repeated in chapter eight, and the meaning here and there is one. In His justice God allows punishment and retribution upon the wicked, and in His mercy He makes this punishment not destroy everyone but the lesser part, and calls the greater part (the two thirds) to return, repent and enjoy His mercies.

entries.section: (3) The sixth trumpet and the second woe

paragraphs.text: The number of the warriors in this woe is two hundred million, and the expression "I heard the number of them" means that God willed for us, through the Saint, to know the number, which is a vast and enormous number. The purpose of mentioning it is to know the severity and power of this woe and its devastating results ... The exact number mentioned is not what is meant, but it signifies that their number is very great.

We believers must not be terrified by the frightening and continuous wars of the demons, but must fortify ourselves with God's promises to His children, for no one can take us from His hand or touch us with harm, because those who are with us are always more than those who are against us ... God's promises are true, and all who love His holy name rely on them until He fulfills for us the proclamation of salvation at His glorious Second Coming ... Amen.

entries.section: (4) The force of the blow, and the refusal of repentance

paragraphs.text: St. John begins to explain the scene of the armies and sees in it the following:
The horses and them that sat on them: the rider's sitting on the steed means the state of final readiness to enter the war.
Breastplates of fire: that is, the war is burning, without mercy or respite.

Jacinth: blue, having the color of the sky. The meaning is either that they come in the appearance of the heavenly beings to deceive people, or that the color of the sky means, in the view of some, the divine permission of this war.

Brimstone: a symbol of the divine wrath, which when it burned Sodom and Gomorrah burned them with fire and brimstone (Gen 19:24). The heads of lions: the head of the horse is of a gentle appearance, and for this reason St. John saw it in a more terrifying, devouring and destructive appearance, as they became the heads of lions.
Fire and smoke and brimstone: they refer to the hosts of the demons in their nature and in what they cause to others during their war.

entries.section: (4) The force of the blow, and the refusal of repentance

paragraphs.text: By these three (the fire, the smoke and the brimstone): that is, by what the demons stir up. The forces of evil, with their various weapons (v. 17), were able to destroy a great number of people, but the mercies of God preserved the two thirds, perhaps that those who remain may understand, return and repent.

entries.section: (4) The force of the blow, and the refusal of repentance

paragraphs.text: Their power is in their mouth: that is, their false, honeyed speech.
Their tails: their tails are like the tails of poisonous scorpions.

This scene pictures and explains to us where the strength of Satan lies. It is first in his mouth and his deceptive speech, and it was the first weapon he used against man when by his lie he brought down Adam and Eve (Gen 3:5). His strength lies also in his tails, which carry the poisons of lusts, so that if he stings with them an incautious person, lust possesses him and becomes in his veins like deadly poison until he dies and perishes spiritually. He fights man from every direction and with many kinds of wars.

Their tails had heads: this means that before Satan stings man with these lusts and sins, he first uses logic (the heads) to persuade the man, to justify the sin and to make him doubt the punishment and judgment, so that he slips into it, overcome and obedient to it.

entries.section: (4) The force of the blow, and the refusal of repentance

paragraphs.text: And the rest of the men: that is, the two thirds who escaped this woe, instead of repenting and returning, became more deviant, so Satan and evil possessed them in various forms.
Gold and silver: that is, people worshipped and craved wealth, riches and material luxury, which is one of the forms of the worship of Satan.

Brass and stone and wood: that is, possessions, houses, palaces and material luxury. What is meant here is people's turning away from God and being occupied with the perishing things of earth rather than the heavenly things. And God shows us, in a gentle rebuking manner, that all of them are things without benefit and without life, for they neither see nor hear, and they remind us of what God said to us before: "They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water" (Jer 2:13).

entries.section: (4) The force of the blow, and the refusal of repentance

paragraphs.text: People continued in their evil and did not repent, nor did they benefit from the woe of the sixth trumpet, but continued in all their sins, such as adultery, theft and others. This means that most of the living people deviated from God, and those who still keep their faith and pure conduct are few, so that the general scene of mankind is distance from God.

My God ... Satan is very cruel in his wars and in his destruction of mankind ... but what terrifies me here is the hardness of my heart and its failure to realize what is going on around it and what is happening to it, so that it does not understand the evil that befalls it, but increases in deviation and in straying after Satan and his deception ... I beg You, my God, rescue us from this evil enemy and from our weaknesses and from every lust and uncleanness that separates us from Your goodness, O Lover of mankind.

The angel clothed with a cloud and the open book, introduction to chapter ten: after the sixth trumpet (ch. 9) and before the seventh trumpet (ch. 11:15), we find that the Book of Revelation presents us with two interjected visions. The first, which comprises "chapter ten," has as its subject the appearance of a mighty angel and a reference to thunders uttered beforehand, while the second vision concerns the appearance of the two witnesses (ch. 11:1-14). Each of these visions has its significances and meanings, and after them we return to the next trumpet, as we mentioned.
I saw another angel: most interpreters saw that this angel is the Lord Christ Himself in one of the appearances in the Book of Revelation, through the following attributes:
Mighty: for He is the owner of all might and authority, indeed their source.
Come down from heaven: that is, from His throne and His position in the bosom of the Father.

Clothed with a cloud: this is the scene by which Christ described Himself in His Second Coming, "they shall see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory" (Lk 21:27). A rainbow upon his head: this is the same scene we saw around the throne in (ch. 4:3), so it is a scene connected with the glory of Christ.

His face was as it were the sun: this is what was said of the Lord Christ Himself at the Transfiguration, "and his face did shine as the sun" (Mt 17:2). And his feet as pillars of fire: the same description of the Lord Christ in (Rev 1:15), meaning feet that are firm and crushing to His enemies.

In His appearance He was carrying a little book open, which means that He wants to give us His few words, which nonetheless open the eyes and the heart and give eternal life to whoever acquires them and acts on them. His feet on the sea and on the land: a scene that indicates the comprehensiveness of His effective authority over the earth, the sea and all creation, or as we say in the words of the Divine Liturgy, "the heaven, the earth, the sea and all that is in them ..."

He cried with a loud voice: if the sixth trumpet was a symbol of the beginning of the fierce war of the Antichrist and the bearing of very hard woes (ch. 9 ...), the voice of Christ came like the voice of a conquering lion, announcing Himself and giving strength, victory and reassurance to His children amid these hard and terrifying events.

When he had cried ... at the end of His mighty voice the seer (St. John) heard the voice of seven thunders. Because thunders are tremendous, frightening sounds, they point to clear and awesome prophecies about the punishment of the wicked.

This voice always reaches us in times of hard trials, on the tongues of His faithful children in every age, so that our hope in Him is renewed, or by direct revelations that He permits to us, such as the apparition of the holy Virgin at Zeitoun in 1968, so that the woes have no authority over us ... but His mighty voice comforts our souls in their weakness. Would that when we hear the voice of God supporting us, we draw near to Him and increase in our prayers and readings, so that they may be a fortification for us against any tribulations to come.

The task of St. John was to write everything he sees of the various visions throughout this book (ch. 1:19), but when he set about writing what he saw and what he heard of what these seven thunders spoke, the divine command came to him which stopped him from writing what he heard and saw, but to be content with sealing them up. Seal up: an imperative verb meaning close them up, or keep secret what they contain.

This command reminds us of what God commanded Daniel also, when He commanded him, saying, "Wherefore shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days" (Dan 8:26). And since God did not permit John to write, and therefore did not permit us to know, it is not for us to strive or guess what these thunders contained ... but rather to submit to the wisdom and judgment of God in absolute trust.
John returns again to the scene of the angel (Christ) whom he saw, and reminds us of His authority over creation, "standing upon the sea and upon the earth."

Lifted up his hand to heaven: as a symbolic reference to God His Father (the hypostasis of the Father), as a preface to what He is about to say. Sware by him that liveth: that is, He called upon the name of the Father as witness, and the expression "sware" is to confirm the decision issued by God, which He is about to announce to us.

That there should be time no longer: that is, the end is about to come quickly, and time will not be prolonged after these times and events. Note: a few interpreters, who do not incline to hold that this angel is Christ, also see that the words "sware by him that liveth" do not come from Christ but from an angel who swears by the name of God ... They also say that all the preceding attributes in the description of him in verses (1-3) may belong to an angel of the principalities who took on the splendor of the One who sent him ...
We have seen that it is honest to present both interpretations.

When the seventh angel is "about" to sound, the appointed time comes that all the faithful servants of God awaited and that He foretold to them in (Mt 24) when He spoke of His Second Coming, and He encouraged the martyrs by their waiting a little season (ch. 6:9-11). What is meant, of course, is the beginning of eternity and the endless reign of Christ.

God in His tenderness does not allow hard tribulations to be long, so He brings relief and deliverance quickly, and however many tribulations the days of our life contain, they will be followed by bliss and joy that cannot be expressed. So support us, our God, that we may look to the coming bliss and bear with thanksgiving all that passes over us, and stand firm in our faith and striving to the end.

And the voice which I heard from heaven: St. John heard voices from heaven many times, sometimes from Christ Himself as in (chs. 1, 2, 3, 4) and sometimes from angels as in (chs. 5, 6, 7); and so we say here that this voice, which indicates that he had heard it before ... is either a voice from God or the voice of another by His command.

Take the little book: the command issued to John was clear, namely to go forward and take this little book and all it contains of prophecies or events from the hand of the angel of whom we spoke in (v. 2).
John obeyed and went, and God permitted him to take it, that is, to know it.
Eat it up: that is, understand it well, absorb it and discover what it contains of prophecies and events.
