It shall make thy belly bitter: that is, what you will come to know about some conditions, such as the persecution of the Church or the apostasy and turning away of people from Christ, will grieve your heart and your soul will become pained, "bitter." The meaning may also point to the pains of service that the faithful servant meets in his service.

In thy mouth sweet as honey: because preaching in the name of Christ is a joyful work, even if it contains pain and toil. It also means that this little book, though it carries bitter news about the Church and her wars, also contains in it sweet and reassuring revelations about the continuity of Christ's work in her and the proclamation of her final victory.

This verse is an explanation of the previous verse, for St. John accomplished what he was commanded and found exactly what he was promised ... It is noted that the expressions the divine inspiration used in these two verses agree completely with what He announced earlier to the prophet Ezekiel in (ch. 3:3, ch. 2:10), for he also ate a book and found in his mouth sweetness as honey, while inside him were "lamentations, and mourning, and woe."

God makes clear to John that he must continue in his work of preaching and evangelizing, whatever the bitterness of the soul and the wars of the obstinate. It is a work not limited to a particular people or a specific kingdom but for all people in every age, and it is a work that goes beyond St. John himself to every servant, priest and bishop, so that we care nothing for any toil, nor even for our own souls or their comfort, for the sake of accomplishing what God charges us with.

Give us, O God, this fiery heart that knows no discouragement, and if the bitterness in our bellies increases, let us not forget the taste of Your sweet word in our mouths. Strengthen us and help us, and give victory to Your Church and Your flock ... Amen.
The two prophets and the resistance to the beast (the Antichrist)

A reed like unto a rod: a measure for measuring lengths, like the meter or the yard at the present time. John was given a rod for measuring lengths and was commanded by the angel to measure the temple and the altar, which are the holiest parts of the Jewish temple of old, and also to measure those who worship there, meaning to count their number. Those who worship are the children of God who worship Him in His Church, and their most important feature is humility.

The court which is without: it was the outer part of the Jewish temple and was not as important as the place of the altar referred to in the previous verse. As for the spiritual meaning, the angel commanded St. John not to measure the outer part, that is, those outside the faith (the Gentiles), defiled by their sins and their evil thoughts, who become a cause of defilement and stumbling for the world that God wants to be holy to Him, "the holy city." Their stumbling continues for forty-two months, which is the period of the Antichrist's dominion and his evils. The three and a half years are half of seven, the number that symbolizes perfection, and so we can say that it is a period that will not be very long. No one can affirm whether this is a real time or a symbolic, prophetic time.

God feels for you in the midst of your tribulations. You are one of His children; He cares for you and for your relationship with His Church, and He keeps the wicked away from you however much they surround you. He also does not allow the tribulation to be long, but supports you until you come out of it and enjoy His blessings and heavenly glories.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: Since the period of the dominion of evil, that is, of the Antichrist, is three and a half years, God sends a special and very powerful grace, namely two witnesses (prophets) who prophesy and support the Church during the same period, for the one thousand two hundred and sixty days are the same as the time of three and a half years (considering the Jewish year to be 360 days). My two witnesses: the Orthodox Church sees in the interpretations of her Fathers that these two witnesses are "Elijah and Enoch," since neither of them died but were taken up to heaven, and they will taste bodily death in (v. 8), as will come.
Clothed in sackcloth: a sign of their grief at what the state of things on earth has come to, and what has befallen many of the believers, and the severity of the war of the beast (the Antichrist).

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: The two olive trees and the two candlesticks: a description of the two prophets. The olive signifies peace, safety and life, just as the dove came in the days of Noah carrying an olive branch as a sign of the end of the Flood, and likewise the lampstand signifies the Church, witnessing to her Christ by the lights of her teaching.

Before the Lord: that is, everything they speak is for the Lord, its source is the Lord, and it is with the blessing and support of God. They will not flatter anyone, for their teaching is frank, pure and clear.

Give me, O God, the spirit of Elijah and Enoch, that I may witness to Your name and proclaim Your truth, so that Your commandment may be raised and exalted above the blasphemy of the world, and do not let me fear or be afraid of anything except Your wrath ... Help me, Lord, for I am weak.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: The Lord gave them authority for the whole time of their ministry on earth, and this authority is referred to by fire coming out of their mouth, because the words that come out of their mouths consume every false teaching or doubt from Satan and his helpers ... The expression of fire coming out of their words reminds us of what actually happened between Elijah and the messenger of King Ahaziah when Elijah rebuked him, "and there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty" (2 Kgs 1:
1-12.) No one can approach them, for whoever approaches them, his end is destruction.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: Part of the strength of their authority is also that God gave them authority to shut heaven, that is, to withhold its goods, and this also reminds us of what Elijah did in shutting heaven from rain for three and a half years (1 Kgs 17:1) in the days of the wicked King Ahab. They also have the authority and power of God that He gave to Moses when he turned the waters of the Nile into blood (Ex 7:20). The overall meaning of the two verses (5, 6) is that God gave them authority and power exceeding every power of men, to do what they wish upon the whole face of the earth.

Does this not remind us, beloved, of the authority God deposited in His Church for the forgiveness of the sins of the penitent through the sacrament of the priesthood and the sacrament of confession, when He said to His pure Apostles, "Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven" (Mt 18:18)? So seize this opportunity, my brother, and enjoy this authority, that you may obtain God's forgiveness and a place in heaven.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: When they shall have finished their testimony: that is, the end of the period set by God for their coming down, their resistance to Satan and their witness.

The beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit: Satan himself with all his power and authority, and the abyss, that is, Hades, is the place of his kingdom and authority and a clear indication of his nature.

Shall make war against them, and shall overcome them: after Satan saw what these two prophets did, it was given to him, by God's permission, to gather all the forces of evil and be able to kill the two prophets, but his authority is limited, for it is over bodies only and not spirits. Let us remember the saying of our Lord, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul" (Mt 10:28).

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: The great city: great in the eyes of evil and the wicked because it symbolizes the authority of Satan and his works in it.
Which spiritually is called: resembles or symbolizes.

Sodom and Egypt: Sodom and Egypt of old symbolized the wicked pagan kingdoms that resisted God. Where also our Lord was crucified: of course Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, but because the meaning is spiritual, what is meant by the general sense of the verse is that the evil latent in the world that rejects God, which by its evil crucified the Lord of glory, believing it had triumphed over Him, is the very same evil that killed these two prophets.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: The wicked gather from every direction, nation and place to gaze, without pity but with every gloating, at the state of these two prophets after their death, as though evil wants to satisfy its rage against these two witnesses who troubled it throughout the former time. From the excess of evil's cruelty, it left the corpses and did not bury them for three and a half days, and this period may be real time or figurative ... but it is a short time.

Among the displays of gloating ... is that the kingdom of evil, with all its members, congratulate one another on the killing of the two prophets and send gifts, as though what happened were a feast and a victory for them.

Because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth: the reason and cause of the joy of the evil world is that it has been relieved of the rebuke, reproof and warnings that the two prophets carried to them, and also of some of the blows they brought down on the world because of its evil (v. 6).

So it is with the wicked in every age. Instead of responding to the warnings of God and His disciplines that He sends through the mouth of His saints and faithful servants, the wicked often want to be rid of them because they alert people and try to turn them away from the way of Satan, as happened with St. John the Baptist, St. John Chrysostom and Pope Athanasius the Apostolic. I beg You, my God, make my heart always obedient to Your voice and submissive to it ... and remove from it all hardness, refusal and stubbornness.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: After the short joy that the wicked enjoyed in their gloating (three and a half days), God restored them to life by His power and in a miraculous way. Just as His glorious Resurrection was an earthquake to the whole kingdom of evil, so also the resurrection of the two witnessing prophets caused great fear and terror among the pillars of the wicked world, which had been arrogantly contemplating its false victory over them.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: They heard a great voice from heaven: God, who honors His faithful holy children, proclaims His honoring of them by calling to them to ascend to heaven, and they ascended to heaven after the pattern of the ascension of the Lord Himself in a cloud (Acts 1:9). As the disciples saw the ascension of Christ, the wicked enemies saw their ascension, so it was a victory and a crown for the two prophets and shame and disgrace for the kingdom of evil.

I thank You, Lord, because even if evil triumphs for a time, its end is known, and even if it seems to us that it has authority over Your children, Your strong hand gives them resurrection, glory, honor and a proclamation of their holiness even after their death, as happened with many of the holy martyrs.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: The same hour: that is, the moment of the ascension of the two witnesses to heaven.
A great earthquake: a figure for the proclamation of the wrath and anger of God on the wicked and the beast.

The tenth part of the city: that is, this was a relative vengeance from God, but the general judgment has not yet come. At the ascension of the witnesses to heaven God shows something of His wrath on the kingdom of evil, so a great earthquake occurs that shakes its pillars and foundations, and a tenth of the wicked people fall, whom St. John estimates at seven thousand. The number here is of course symbolic and means relative multitude, since seven and a thousand are numbers of perfection. Names of men: this means that God in His just judgment knows exactly to whom He directs His blow, as though this vengeance were directed to people known by name to God.
Gave glory: the fear and terror that seized the wicked wrung from them a confession of the power of the God of these two witnesses, so they offered Him glorification and knew that He is the true God.

entries.section: (2) The sending of the two prophets

paragraphs.text: The first woe was the blow of the locusts (ch. 8:13), and the second woe carried the blow of the armies of horsemen (ch. 9:12) and also the blows of the two witnessing prophets. With the end of their story the inspired text announces the end of the second woe, but it alerts us to the existence of a third woe.

The talk about the angel of the sixth trumpet ended at the end of chapter nine, and chapter ten and chapter eleven up to the previous verse contained interjected events, and we now return to the seventh angel and the last trumpet.

When the seventh angel sounded, a proclamation was made in heaven with great jubilation, in which all the heavenly creation took part, of the end of the events and the wrathful, disciplining blows. Now has come the proclamation of the final victory over the kingdom of evil, and the whole world has become subject to the authority of God the Father and His only-begotten Son, who announced with voices of glorification the beginning of His endless reign.
Vv. 16, 17 The four: and twenty priests: (see ch. 4:4).

Fell upon their faces and worshipped: the twenty-four priests, as they did before (ch. 4:10), offering praise, thanksgiving and honor. This time the subject of their praise was the offering of thanks for the work of God in punishing the kingdom of evil and refuting it, in spreading His reign, in the return of the world to faith, and in the proclamation of God's infinite power in making and ordering all this.
Thou hast taken to thee thy great power: that is, it was always Yours, but You proclaimed it at the appropriate time.

The wicked nations were angry and Your Church suffered for a time because of them, but the anger of the nations is counted as nothing before You, for Your wrath is what everyone should fear, and it is what has happened and indeed come. The time of the dead: that is, the time of the wicked and their judgment.
Thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants: that is, the recompense and the inheritance of the Kingdom.
This reward included:
The prophets: that is, those who witnessed and served the word of God and conveyed it and interpreted it to people.
The saints: everyone who walked in the fear of God, trying to please Him by carrying out His commandments.
Them that fear thy name: everyone who set the fear of God before him so as not to sin.
Small and great: that is, all who followed You, whatever their standing or age.
As for those who wearied the earth and destroyed many by their evils, they will receive the like of what they did, that is, God's justice requires their eternal destruction.
The temple of God was opened in heaven: that is, the perfect glory of God in eternity was proclaimed, and it means the entrance of the righteous believers to enjoy eternal existence with Him.

There was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: the ark of the covenant always symbolized the continual presence of God in the midst of His people, and the appearance of the ark of the covenant here means confirmation of the opening of the temple and everyone's enjoyment of this presence and constant standing before God.

There were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail: in this part of the verse there are two meanings. The first makes clear that being in the divine presence is an awesome presence, for all these phenomena are connected with the divine glory. The second meaning is that the temple of God, in which His children enjoy being with Him, is itself the source of His justice, and from it come His judgments and punishments for the wicked, and this agrees with the word "hail," since whenever it appears in the Holy Bible it mostly carries the meaning of punishment.

My God, how beautiful it is to be with You and to enjoy You in Your heavenly temple ... and You have also granted us to stand in Your holy temple in Your Church here, so that we are counted as those standing in heaven, as though we are receiving a pledge of the everlasting eternal glory ... Make us worthy, my Lord, to complete the days of our bodily sojourn in Your fear and Your favor, that we may enjoy what You prepared for us before the foundation of the world.

Satan resists the Church, a general introduction: the second and thirteenth chapters include a scene picturing the Church and her wars with Satan in three images: the first with the dragon, whose origin was from heaven; the second with a beast coming up out of the sea; and the third with a beast coming up out of the earth. The general meaning of the two chapters is that Satan's war against the Church is a perpetual war from her birth and in every place.
A great wonder: a marvelous scene and event.

A woman clothed with the sun: the Church wrapped in her Christ (the Sun of righteousness). The moon under her feet: the moon here may symbolize the bodies and relics of the saints and the stories of their labors, on which the Church stands, so that she increases in splendor and beauty.

Upon her head a crown: the crown always signifies kingship and authority ... and the twelve stars (that is, the Apostles, the pure disciples of Christ) are her authority, her preaching and the secret of her priesthood.

The meaning that the first verse carries as a whole is a radiant picture of the Church, which declares that the secret of her strength is her attachment to Christ, the true Light, borne up by faith, striving and the radiance of the virtues of her saints, and her authority is in the power of the sacrament of her priesthood, handed down from Christ to the pure Apostles by His pure, holy breathing. This woman also signifies the Virgin Mary and her Son Christ, as the Thursday praise in our Church mentions. She also signifies the soul that loves God, which Satan wars against and which brings forth many virtues in Christ.
She cried, travailing in birth: the severe pains of childbirth.

From her first days the Church is a mature mother able to give birth, and her pains point to her constant striving to bring forth "God the Word" in the hearts of her children, or in other words to bring forth children strong in the faith.
Another wonder: another event.
A great red dragon: a reference to Satan in his evil, his severity and his bloodthirstiness.
Seven heads: a reference to the power of his thoughts, and their multiplicity and variety.
Ten horns: the horn in an animal represents its strength in attack, and ten horns means that he uses all his strength and energies.
Seven crowns upon his heads: that is, he has authority over his children and his soldiers and those who follow him in the whole world.
His tail: his tail.

In some creatures the tail is considered the strongest thing in them (like the crocodile or the scorpion), and the verse here is a continuation of the explanation of Satan's strength, describing his tail with the strength by which he was able to bring down the angels who followed him at his fall. The mention of the number of a third is a reference to his strength on the one hand, but also that those he was able to bring down are a limited number, since two thirds remained.
Stood before the woman: he announces his challenge to the Church.

To devour her child: the child here is a direct reference to the Lord Christ Himself, whom the Church wants to bring forth in her children, and Satan lies in wait for His birth in order to kill the work of the Church in preaching Christ.

The meaning here is clear and direct and admits only the person of Christ Himself, whom Satan wanted to swallow by death, but He swallowed death. He is the One of whom David prophesied, "I will give thee the heathen for thine inheritance ... Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron" (Ps 2:9). To rule all nations: that is, He accepts everyone from every place so long as they believe in Him and in His commandments.
A rod of iron: it shows the strength of His authority over His enemies.
Caught up unto God, and to his throne: a reference to His Resurrection, His Ascension and His sitting at the right hand of the Father.
The woman fled: that is, she went far away and escaped the harm of Satan.

The Church finds her rest in the wilderness, away from the world of sin, where her God sustains her completely, as He sustained Elijah and sustained His people for the forty years in the wilderness of Sinai. The wilderness also points to austerity and renunciation of the world and its pleasures. As long as a person is detached and limited in his needs, he can nullify the wars of Satan, since material things lose their authority over him.

A place prepared: that is, God, by His foreknowledge, prepared for her everything she needs throughout the time of her sojourn away from the world. A thousand two hundred ...: it signifies the short time that is followed by eternity (see ch. 11:3).

My beloved God ... the love of the world often hinders us and keeps us from setting out to You and enjoying You. Blessed are the fathers of the wilderness, who left everything for Your sake ...; grant us also to leave what occupies us away from You, that we too may win Your companionship.

entries.section: (2) The casting out of Satan from heaven

paragraphs.text: Many of the Fathers saw that this whole scene, that is, these three verses, speaks of things that happened before the creation of man, and therefore this war is a war waged by the archangel Michael against Satan and all his followers whom he led astray, and Michael was able to cast them all out, because it is not reasonable for Satan to remain after his fall standing before God among His luminous creation. Those who hold this opinion prove it by what came in the Book of Job when God asked Satan, "Whence comest thou?" and Satan answered, "From going to and fro in the earth" (Job 1:7). The meaning of this is that Satan's authority became confined to the earth after his fall and expulsion.

As for the other opinion in interpretation, it avoids fixing the time of this scene and considers that what John saw here represents heaven's support of the Church in her war against Satan in the time of her sojourn, so that Satan's power is greatly diminished. This expression is very consoling to the Church, for despite the power of the dragon, he is weaker than the archangel Michael and his angels.
The great dragon: an expression indicating the strength of Satan.

That old serpent: this is also his title after he took the form of the serpent when he seduced Adam and Eve. Satan: the best-known of his names, and it is Hebrew, meaning "the adversary or the opponent." The Devil: his Greek name, meaning "the accuser."

Which deceiveth the whole world: by his deception and people's believing him, since he is "a liar, and the father of it" (Jn 8:44). Cast out into the earth: a reference to the fact that his power is limited before the archangel Michael, who defeated him and cast him out.

God in His love supports us in our striving by the intercessions of the angels on our behalf and their help to us in all our works. Would that we make use of this love and establish friendship with them, so that we are strengthened and advance with confidence in our spiritual life.

entries.section: (2) The casting out of Satan from heaven

paragraphs.text: I heard a loud voice: a new proclamation in a raised voice, made by one of the angels.
Now is come salvation of our God: that is, the salvation of all who believe in His name, and salvation is ascribed to God because it is He who offered it to mankind.

The accuser is cast down: that is, Satan is cast out (v. 9). Accused them: that is, Satan's work is accusing, envying the children of God and fighting them, as in (Job 1:11). Day and night: a figure for Satan's perseverance and diligence in ensnaring the children of God. With the fall of Satan from heaven and his confinement to the earth, the heavenly creation proclaimed its glorification of God the Father and His Christ, that is, His only-begotten Son, and this glorification consists of thanking God for His victory and His plan of salvation through His Son the Redeemer, and the proclamation of His sole and everlasting reign and authority.

entries.section: (2) The casting out of Satan from heaven

paragraphs.text: They overcame him: that is, the victory was accomplished for the children of God.
By the blood of the Lamb: that is, the blood of Christ shed on the wood of the Cross and offered to the world for salvation.

By the word of their testimony: that is, the faith that they accepted and preached, and suffered for, and perhaps were martyred for. This verse presents the secret of the victory of the believing children of God. They took refuge in the blood of Christ poured out for them, through their faith in the power and effectiveness of this blood for salvation and through the sacrament of the Eucharist, in which Christ gives us His precious and most holy Blood. Their lives also became a witness to Christ in all their conduct and in bearing the pains of persecution, whatever they were. St. John gives us the reason for their endurance and steadfastness, which is that they loved their God Christ more than their lives, so they cared nothing for what happened to them, even if it was death itself.

entries.section: (2) The casting out of Satan from heaven

paragraphs.text: Therefore: that is, because of the proclamation of salvation and the authority of Christ (v. 10) and because of the victory of the children of God (v. 11).

The invitation to joy and jubilation was addressed to the heavenly creation with all that is in it, because of the preceding events: the casting down of Satan to the earth and his confinement, the proclamation of the victory and authority of Christ, and likewise the victory of all His children through their acceptance of faith in the effectiveness of His blood for salvation.
Woe to the inhabiters of the earth: that is, a warning to all the inhabitants of the earth of the severity of what is to come ...

Since Satan knew that he has a short time before the Second Coming of Christ and the proclamation of the general judgment, the wrath of his failure became great, like a wounded animal, and for this reason he is about to pour out his wrath on the Church in various and severe wars.

entries.section: (3) The war on the earthly Church

paragraphs.text: Exactly what was warned of in the previous verse (v. 12) took place, but God by His grace gave the Church two wings with which she can rise above all the wars of Satan: "They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles" (Isa 40:31). These two wings are the subject of the meditations of many of the Fathers, and among them are those who saw:

a) That they are the two Testaments (Old and New), by which a person rises to the lofty heavens of contemplation. b) Or that they are faith and works, which are the two wings of salvation and of reaching the Kingdom. c) Or that they are the greatest commandments, of loving God with all the heart and a person's loving his fellow man. d) Some also saw that they are the pure wings of prayer and fasting, by which the worship of God is made upright. Fly into the wilderness, where she is nourished: see (v. 6). For a time, and times, and half a time: as in (v. 6) also, with a difference in expression, for the word time means a year, so the meaning is (a year + two years + half a year), that is, three and a half years or one thousand two hundred and sixty days ... This time has been repeated often and always means a limited period, since it is half of the number seven, which indicates perfection ... The meaning intended as a whole is that the Church will be kept in the wilderness that God prepared for her throughout the time of her persecution, which is relatively short compared with the times of glory in eternity.

entries.section: (3) The war on the earthly Church

paragraphs.text: In a new war to drown the Church in the world, Satan cast out of his mouth much water "as a flood." These waters point to the many wicked multitudes of the world who want to carry the Church away from the wilderness, the place of her sustenance and her God's care, and draw her into the world and its lusts, for Satan knows perfectly well that if the Church leaves her wilderness (v. 6) she loses all her strength.

entries.section: (3) The war on the earthly Church

paragraphs.text: The earth helped the woman: that is, God by His power made some of the inhabitants of the earth stand before Satan and defend His Church.

Some saw that this river (v. 15) is the river of Jewish and Roman persecution, and the help that came from the earth was the stopping of this persecution by the decree of the Emperor Constantine and the recognition of Christianity as one of the religions acknowledged in the ancient Roman state.

The general spiritual meaning is that the Church is kept in God's plan throughout the time of her sojourn on earth, and God by His power is able to raise up from among her opponents defenders of her, so that He scatters all the wars of the evil Satan.

entries.section: (3) The war on the earthly Church

paragraphs.text: Satan's rage at the failure of his attempts continued, but this anger did not dissuade him from continuing the war with the children of God and the Church, especially those who hold fast to keeping the commandments of Christ and acting on them.

I thank You, my Lord Jesus Christ, for You have revealed to us the secret of the Church's victory and gave us victory with her. Our strength is in Your sustaining and Your spiritual food offered to us in the wilderness, which, if the Church leaves it, she loses everything with it, and when she holds fast to it she nullifies all the wars of the evil enemy and triumphs over him. I thank You for these verses that encourage the soul in its striving throughout the time of its sojourn.

The two beasts, a general introduction: this chapter speaks of two beasts who are followers of the great dragon mentioned in (ch. 12), and who form with him a trinity whose whole aim is the destruction and deception of people. Since the dragon's first war was in heaven, the two beasts, his followers, one (came out of the sea) and the other (out of the earth), as a figure for the severity of Satan's war and its comprehensiveness!!...

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: I stood upon the sand of the sea: a preface to the fact that what he is about to see comes from the sea. The sand points to instability and lack of steadfastness, the sea to turbulence, and its waves to the multitudes of the wicked.
I saw a beast: a creature came out of the sea, and he described it as a beast because of its great evil.

Having seven heads and ten horns: see the explanation of the dragon in the previous chapter (v. 3). What draws our attention is the identity of the form of this beast with the dragon, and this means the identity of their aims, intentions and also their ferocity.

Some interpreters see that the seven heads and ten horns are seven nations and ten successive kings who support Satan and extend his authority, and they prove this by the crowns upon his heads, which only kings wear. Some of them explained that the ten horns and their crowns are the ten Roman emperors in their war on the Church, beginning with Nero and ending with Diocletian, which is the worst period of persecution the whole Church has witnessed. Upon his heads the name of blasphemy: whoever this beast is, his aim, which God reveals to us, is to blaspheme the name of God the Most High in order to lead people astray.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: Like unto a leopard: in the swiftness of its pouncing, its ferocity and its treachery, for the leopard is an animal that preys on anything even if it is not hungry.

His feet were as the feet of a bear: the bear is a huge, heavy animal that sometimes walks on four and sometimes stands on its hind legs (its feet) ... The meaning is that the beast is like the bear when it displays its strength, standing and resting on its two strong legs.
His mouth as the mouth of a lion: that is, with the strength of its jaw when it closes upon prey.
And the dragon gave him: that is, the chief of the demons gave this beast, or these kingdoms, all his power and authority in the war against the Church and the children of God.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: I saw one of his heads: that is, one of the seven heads.
As it were wounded: that is, it was not slain but plays a part in order to lead people astray, pretending weakness for a purpose of its own that we shall come to know.

His deadly wound was healed: that is, what the world supposed of death in him was not real, for he rose again with a power that astonished all the inhabitants of the earth, so that they offered Satan and his followers prostration and worship and the confession that they are the true power that cannot be overcome.

The spiritual meaning of these two verses is that Satan may pretend weakness for a short time in order to deceive the children of God, that perhaps they may become negligent in their striving, then he rises with force again, trying to devour them, and displays his strength so as to make the world follow him all the more and increase in its error and its denial of the power of God.

Beware, beloved, for there is no truce with the enemy in your striving and the days of your sojourn, and do not be amazed by the signs or miracles that Satan may bring in order to lead you astray, even if he imitates Christ in His death and resurrection, for he has no purpose but your destruction.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: There was given unto him a mouth: that is, his power is not from himself, but God permitted him to use this power that Satan gave him.
Great things and blasphemies: that is, everything that attracts people on the one hand and everything that makes them doubt God on the other.
Power was given unto him: everything is by God's permission.

Forty and two months: that is, three and a half years, which is the time of the Church's sojourn in the wilderness (ch. 12:6), yet this period is a set period, just as the authority of Satan, however severe, is also limited.
Satan gave the beast of the sea power to blaspheme against God, and God permitted that for a limited time, which is 42 months.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: He opened his mouth in blasphemy against God: he blasphemes the name of God, that is, he directs insults at the name of God, or it also means that he takes titles of God and ascribes them to himself.
His tabernacle: that is, he mocks the Church and makes the world scoff at her.
Them that dwell in heaven: he makes people doubt eternity and the other life with ideas of atheism and rational doubt.

The general meaning is that he fights without rest on all fronts: he attacks the name of God and transgresses against it, and attacks also His Church and the children of God who dwell with Him, and also mocks heaven and eternal life. My beloved brother: is this not what is happening now around us in the world, of Satan's success in attacking God and His Church in what they call the civilized world? The world in many places now claims that God is merely a myth in people's minds, and many European countries now proudly declare that they are secular states that have no connection with religion or Christianity ... Would that we learn to pray for the salvation of the world and the overthrow of the power of the evil Satan.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: God also permitted the beast to make war with the children of God, that is, the saints.
To overcome them: that is, to kill whoever does not worship him. It is an apparent victory, but this takes nothing from their salvation and their heavenly inheritance.
Over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations: that is, the spread of his error, his blasphemy and his war in the whole world.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: Part of the power of this beast is that everyone will submit to him, worship him and bow down to him, except the children of God. Whose names are written: that is, the children of God who are known to Him, whose names He kept in the book of life by His foreknowledge and knowledge of their striving, their holding fast to faith in Him and their resistance to Satan. This book of life, that is, eternal salvation, is ascribed to the slain Lamb, because there is no salvation or eternity outside faith in the blood of Christ.

Part of the power of this beast is that many who are condemned to eternal death will worship him, that is, those who did not believe and enjoy the salvation of Christ and were not written in the book of life.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: If any man have an ear, let him hear: a warning of the importance of what has been said and a drawing of attention to what is coming.

entries.section: (1) The beast rising up out of the sea

paragraphs.text: This verse represents the end of the talk about the first beast with all his power, and the speech here is about God's final recompense to this beast and his kingdoms. Its general meaning is that treatment and judgment are in kind ... so everything the beast brought will turn back upon him.
Goeth into captivity: that is, as he took many captive and imprisoned them, his end will be prison and chains in the abyss.
Must be killed with the sword: God's justice and retribution are necessary in the end, because the end of this beast is destruction.

The speech here is about the second beast and the third enemy and what distinguishes him from the dragon and the first beast: Coming up out of the earth: the earth here symbolizes lowness and degradation, which is fitting for the description of the one who rises out of it.
He had two horns like a lamb: that is, he pretends the meekness of lambs, so that his speech is soft, gentle and attractive.

He spake as a dragon: that is, when he opened his mouth and his real thoughts appeared ... everyone became sure of his cruelty and that he is a beast like his predecessor, wanting nothing but the destruction of all.

All the interpreters agreed that this beast is the false prophet who comes in the time of lambs, as the Lord Christ warned His disciples (Mt 7:15). He "spake," that is, he used logic and lying in leading people astray, yet anyone who has spiritual discernment and sound faith can easily uncover his error.
He exercised all the power of the first beast: that is, he has the same power as the first beast in harming and preying.
Before him: he devotes all his efforts to the service of the first beast, that is, the Antichrist.

By the authority, power and ability to deceive that he has, this beast was able to make the multitudes of mankind bow down to and worship the first beast. The meaning we can draw is that the kingdom of evil with all its demons works in coordination and helps one another, for it is one dark kingdom and its one aim is to turn people away from God and destroy them.

He doeth great wonders: by his magic and his authority he brings what people believe to be extraordinary miracles, so that he imitated what Elijah did when he brought down fire from heaven (1 Kgs 18), with the difference of course that Elijah proclaimed the power of God, while the beast leads people astray. The purpose of all these works is dazzling and frightening, so that people submit to this liar and believe him, and then comes the second step, for which this beast appeared, which is to lead people, indeed to command and compel them, to worship the Antichrist, that is, the first beast. That they should make an image to the beast: that is, replacing the worship of God with the worship of Satan, or wiping the image of God from people's minds, so that nothing remains in their minds but the image of the Antichrist.

Who had the wound by a sword, and did live: the first beast, that is, the Antichrist (v. 3). The beast coming up out of the earth performs miracles such as bringing fire down from heaven to dazzle people and frighten them so that they worship the beast of the sea.

This evil one (the beast of the earth) was able to lead people astray and persuade them of the power of the first beast (the Antichrist) and that he is the true God, and he made an image or form for him, or perhaps by the power of magic he made his image speak and talk. So people believed in him, and everyone who refused and held fast to the sound faith was killed in a great persecution.

As God sealed His faithful servants with the Holy Spirit, that is, with the anointing of the Holy Myron, so also the beast did with his followers of all races, ages and classes, and this mark was: a) On their right hand: that is, he took possession of their will, for the hand represents the will.
b) In their foreheads: that is, he also controlled their minds and thoughts.
It can also be said that by his possessing a person's hand, he cannot raise his hand to make the sign of the Cross on his forehead so as to free his head from the thoughts of Satan and his authority.

Because of Satan's control over people, it became hard for those who refuse his mark, that is, the children of God, to live their lives and obtain their necessities, because the wicked refuse to deal with them. The name or mark of the beast: the sign that distinguishes his followers.
The number of his name: it will be explained in the next verse.

Here is wisdom: that is, knowing the identity of the beast and not being deceived by him and by all that he brings requires great wisdom, whose source is God and which is given only to the faithful who have held fast to the sound faith. The number of the beast .. the number of a man .. Six hundred threescore and six: this number (666) has wearied all the interpreters (to no avail) in their attempt to reach the name of the beast. They attributed the number to the Hebrew letters at one time and the Greek at another, and all of them came out with different conclusions that explained nothing, because the name is in the first place hidden from men, otherwise God would have declared it to them. After reviewing all the opinions of the early Fathers in their interpretation, honesty requires us to take the spiritual interpretation without entering into what we do not know. The number 6 is an incomplete number compared with the number 7, which indicates perfection, or the number 8, which indicates eternity. Accordingly we can say that God wants to reassure us that the first and second beast, and before them the dragon, with all they were able to do and bring, are incomplete and deficient before the divine perfection, and none of them brought anything except by God's permission and wisdom.

God wanted to reveal to us the nature of Satan, so he appeared to us as a dragon or a cruel and deceptive beast ... and we have no escape except taking refuge in the name of God, by calling upon Him and communing with Him, "for the name of the Lord is a strong tower" (Prov 18:10), and by continuing in union with Him through partaking of the Holy Mysteries, so that through Him we have victory over the beast and all his kingdom.

The Lamb and the believers ... and the harvest of the earth, a general introduction: the two preceding chapters showed Satan's resistance to the Church and the children of God with all his power through the dragon and the two beasts, in every place (heaven, sea and earth ...). Here we move to a comforting scene that proclaims the victory of the Lamb and the justice of God, which increases our hope in the time of our difficulties ...
And I looked: a preface to the description of a new scene having no connection with what preceded.

A Lamb: a reference and symbol to the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, for He is the Lamb slain for our redemption. A hundred forty and four thousand: a reference to the multitude of the redeemed who follow Him (see ch. 7:4). His Father's name: as the followers of the beast have a mark that shows their identity and allegiance, so also the children of God have a mark, and the name of God on their foreheads, which is a free gift that we receive here by Baptism and confirm by our striving against sin, and which is completed for us in heaven.

Christ appeared on Mount Zion, which is a figure for the Church and her elevated place, because the temple of the Old Testament was built on this mountain, and also a figure for heaven and its height and the everlasting dwelling place of God (Ps 9:11). With Him also appeared His own, who received Him, believed and held fast to Him ... For God in His love for His children makes them share by His grace in His glories.
The scene of the appearance of the Lord Christ was accompanied by voices originating from heaven, and they are strong voices "
proclaiming His victory, "many waters and thunder," and gentle voices of praise proclaiming the jubilation of the heavenly creation over the Savior " "
the Redeemer, playing on harps. See also (ch. 5:8, 9).
And they sung: that is, the hundred and forty-four thousand with the heavenly creation.

A new song: that is, words that were not known, which the Holy Spirit gives to the victors, and this reminds us of what the Apostle Paul said about the language of heaven, "which it is not lawful for a man to utter" (2 Cor 12:14). Redeemed from the earth: that is, by the blood of Christ, for Christ paid His blood as the price for purchasing everyone who accepts His redemption in all the world ...

This verse shows us the special gifts that are given only to the children of God and to no others. They have the name of God (v. 1), and they now have a language of praise and a song that belongs to them and that none other knows, and they alone stand before the divine throne, always enjoying the sight and presence of God, which cannot be described and cannot be grasped by the human mind.
These two verses show the reason and causes for the distinction of these (the hundred and forty-four thousand) from the rest of the inhabitants of the world, in that they:

1- Lived a life of purity, for the only Bridegroom of their souls is the Lord Christ and their desire is to please Him, and they did not live in the lusts of fornication like the rest of the inhabitants of the world.
2- Follow the Lamb: their eyes and hearts are attached to Him and do not leave Him, for His place is always their place.

3- Were redeemed from among men: they alone are those who accepted faith in Christ and lived as befits this faith, in works that please the heart of God, and became an example and firstfruits for others.

4- In their mouth was found no guile: they imitated the Lamb, their God, "who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" (1 Pet 2:22). All their speech is true, and they are not like the children of the evil world in their cunning and error.

5- Without fault before the throne of God: although there is no man without sin or fault, because of their faithfulness in striving and in trying to please God, God ascribed perfection to them, so that they became without fault before Him.

My God, the Lamb slain for me .. I always desire, despite all my weaknesses, to be without fault before You, but here I am still far from You ... When shall I follow You with all my heart like these saints, and when shall I praise You with such a spiritual song? Grant me, O God, to complete the days of my sojourn in fear, for Your good pleasure, and let me enjoy You here that I may win eternity with You there on the heavenly Mount Zion.

entries.section: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

paragraphs.text: A scene of a new angel flying in the midst of heaven for all the inhabitants of the earth to see, carrying " "

good news, that is, glad tidings for all who await it among the inhabitants of the earth, and at the same time it is frightening news for everyone who ignored and did not believe in the coming of the hour of judgment. His voice was strong and resounding, proclaiming the beginning of the judgment, and because of its awe and severity, prostration and contrition were required before the Owner of this hour, who is God, the Creator of heaven, earth, the sea and all that is in them.
The everlasting gospel: true news with no going back. Some also saw that it is the Holy Bible, which carries all the true promises of God.

entries.section: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

paragraphs.text: A second angel appeared, proclaiming new news, the fall of Babylon!!...

Babylon is fallen, is fallen: Babylon symbolizes the kingdom of evil throughout the ages, and what the angel proclaimed here is the same as what the prophet Isaiah said in his prophecy, "Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods" (Isa 21:9). The meaning is that at the proclamation of God's judgment at His Second Coming, the passing away of the kingdom of Satan, with all its soldiers and power, is also proclaimed, and it will not rise again.

She made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication: this also agrees with what the prophet Jeremiah said, "Babylon hath been a golden cup ... that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine ... Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed" (Jer 51:7, 8). The meaning is that the kingdom of evil did various evils in every direction and caused many to stumble and fall, for Satan in his wrath and rage seduced people with actual bodily fornication and drowned them in destructive lusts, or with spiritual fornication, meaning that he isolated them and separated them from God. This proclamation as a whole carries joy and victory at the end of the evil one, whose day of just judgment has come.

entries.section: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

paragraphs.text: The first angel came proclaiming the salvation of Christ and the believers' enjoyment of Him, and the second proclaimed the just judgment of God and the passing away of the kingdom of evil and its final fall .. and now the third angel comes proclaiming the severe vengeance of God on everyone who followed Satan and became his servant.

If any man worship the beast and his image: that is, whoever worshipped Satan with direct worship, or practiced magic, or called others to leave God and worship Satan, and everyone whom Satan used to cause others to stumble. Receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand: see (ch. 13:16). For all these the punishment of God will be very severe and terrifying.

The wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture: people were accustomed at their feasts to dilute wine with water to weaken its effect, but the word "without mixture" means "strong and concentrated without dilution," which is a figure for the severity of God's punishment of everyone who followed Satan. There is no room for God's mercies in the general judgment for whoever did not make use of them here in his life on earth.
"Shall be tormented with fire and brimstone," which burned Sodom and Gomorrah of old (Gen 19:24), and the expression confirms all that preceded of the severity of God's wrath and punishment.

In the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: as the followers of the beast mocked and made light of heaven, God and all His believing children in His living Church, God's justice requires that His angels and His holy children enjoy the accomplishment of His justice and the defeat of the evil enemy who made them taste much torment and persecution on earth, and Christ Himself will be in the midst of His children, proclaiming His authority and victory.

entries.section: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

paragraphs.text: The smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: a figure for the continuance of their burning without stopping and without their being consumed; for it is known that fire after a period consumes everything, and when it ends the smoke also ends shortly after it .. but here it continues without end.

They have no rest: it was customary to give the tortured a period of rest and breath before resuming their torture, but here there is no rest and no stopping. The expression day and night is figurative, since there is no night and day in eternity, but it denotes the continuance of the torment without interruption.

entries.section: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

paragraphs.text: Here is the patience of the saints: that is, at this time God proclaims and rewards all the saints who were patient and bore all the persecution of the beast, and God shows us their reward to encourage us, making clear that the secret of their victory and patience is the strength of their faith in the Lord Jesus and their striving to act on His commandment.

My beloved brother, the frightening scene of the end of the wicked and likewise God's blessing of His holy, patient children is nothing but a message to us all that carries a warning and an encouragement: the warning of God's stern judgment on the wicked, and the encouragement for us if we stand firm in striving and holding fast to our Christ. Let us therefore hold fast to our striving, whatever the price paid here on earth, and also to our hope in the salvation of our God and His blessing of His faithful servants.

entries.section: (2) The three angels and the proclamation of judgment

paragraphs.text: I heard a voice from heaven: this may be the voice of God or the voice of the angel who accompanied John in his vision.
God proclaims His blessing, that is, the happiness of everyone who leaves life on earth and is transferred to heaven, where their true rest and happiness begin, which is not deficient.

Their works do follow them: God indicates that His justice requires that a person be recompensed for all the works he did in his life, and this is what our Church teaches us in her belief that a person's salvation requires his faith in Christ, and likewise his good works, for which he will be recompensed in eternity with rest, happiness and blessedness.

After that St. John saw the Lord Christ wrapped in His glory, for the cloud always points to the glory of God, His purity and holiness. And because this scene is connected with the authority of the Lord Christ in the judgment of the wicked, St. John saw Him crowned with a crown of gold, as an indication of His everlasting reign. The sickle is a curved agricultural tool, like the crescent, used for reaping crops, and it is a figure for the beginning of the reaping of all mankind, and the whole scene symbolizes the beginning of the judgment. It is noted that this scene agrees completely with what the Lord Christ Himself said about the beginning of the judgment, "But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come" (Mk 4:29).
Another angel came out of the temple: that is, he came out from before God and His presence.

Crying with a loud voice: a great and strong voice, because it suits the subject he speaks about, which is the beginning of the judgment. The word "crying" here means that he pleads earnestly and eagerly with the Lord to begin what the angels have longed to see accomplished, as have all the saints who pray every day with longing, "Thy kingdom come." The harvest of the earth is ripe: the farmer is accustomed to reaping his plants after they dry, like wheat and beans ... that is, the harvest is completely ready and its promised hour has come ...
And thrust in ... his sickle: that is, he proclaimed the beginning of His judgment and the end of life on earth.

The sickle that was in the hand of Christ represents His will and authority at the time of the beginning of the judgment, while the angel who came out with the sickle is a reference to all the angels to whom the command of execution was issued.
Another angel: other than the one carrying the sickle.

From the altar: where the prayers of the saints were with the incense (ch. 8), and where the souls of the martyrs also cried out, "How long, O Lord ... dost thou not judge and avenge our blood" (ch. 6:10). Which had power over fire: this indicates that his redemption was to gather the wicked to their place, which is the fire. The clusters of the vine of the earth: he means the wicked who completed their evils and refused repentance and so deserved the judgment of the earth.
This angel, who is responsible for the place of eternal torment, that is, the fire, proclaims to the angel carrying the sickle to begin the judgment in order to cast the wicked into the eternal fire.
And the angel thrust in his sickle: that is, the first, charged with the other angels to begin the work.
Gathered the vine of the earth: that is, the souls of mankind, which he reaped by death.
The great winepress of the wrath of God: the place prepared for the wicked, and the word winepress suggests the severity of the just divine punishment and vengeance.
The winepress was trodden: that is, the punishment began, and the literal meaning is that the process of pressing began, and the word "trodden" is the expression used for that.

Without the city: the city here is the city of God, His angels and His saints, and "without the city" is a meaning that symbolizes the impossibility of the wicked being in the presence of God during their punishment, for no wicked person approaches the holy place.
Even unto the horse bridles: the blood coming out of the winepress of the wicked became so deep that it rose from the surface of the earth to the horses' bridles, which are placed above their noses.

By the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs: the speech here is all figurative, but the meaning intended is a confirmation of all that preceded of the severity of God's wrath and punishment of the wicked, as though their blood were not contained by a basin whose height is the noses of horses and whose area is hundreds of kilometers!!...

If the day of judgment will certainly come, let us hasten to repentance and reject every lust, however dear it is to us, and cut off all its sources, so that we escape the divine wrath and indeed enjoy His love and tenderness.

Preface to the bowls of God's wrath, introduction to the chapter: this chapter is connected with the one that follows it at one point, which is the seven bowls (plagues) of God's wrath, the last before the judgment. This chapter only refers to them, while the details come in chapter sixteen.

1 And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous, seven angels having the seven last plagues; for in them is filled up the wrath of God. 2 And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass, having the harps of God. 3 And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints. 4 Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest."

5 And after that I looked, and, behold, the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened: 6 And the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues, clothed in pure and white linen, and having their breasts girded with golden girdles. 7 And one of the four beasts gave unto the seven angels seven golden vials full of the wrath of God, who liveth for ever and ever. 8 And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God, and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple, till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled.

I saw another sign: that is, a new vision, other than the seven churches, the seven seals, the seven trumpets and the vision of the dragon and the two beasts. He affirms that it is great and marvelous because of the scenes and meanings it contains. Seven angels .. seven plagues: the number seven points to the perfection and severity of these plagues. They are not like the earlier plagues, for those were for discipline and for man's turning back from his evil, whereas these are for stern punishment.
The last: pointing to the fact that they come immediately before the judgment and nothing follows them ... in them all the wrath and vengeance of God is completed.
St. John saw a great sight: seven angels carrying seven bowls, which are the wrath of God, before the day of judgment.

I saw a sea of glass: this is the same sea that is before the divine throne (ch. 4:6). Glass and crystal signify purity and transparency, for no one can stand in the presence of God unless he is pure and clean.

Mingled with fire: fire signifies the divine justice that pierces, examines and repays. In another interpretation, this fire may point to the sufferings that the children of God pass through during their lives, which qualify them to stand before Him. And them that had gotten the victory over the beast: that is, those who completed the race and the striving and triumphed over Satan and all his marks and followers, and did not submit or bow down to him. See what was said about the marks of the beast and his image (ch. 13). Having the harps of God: that is, God gave them the spirit of prayer and praise, and this is their new angelic work.

In this verse he reassures us, before mentioning God's wrath in the bowls, with a beautiful sight: the children of God who believe in Him, who have triumphed over Satan and stand in purity around the throne of God praising Him.

They sing the song of Moses: when Moses crossed the Red Sea and Pharaoh was drowned, Moses praised God, offering Him glorification and thanksgiving (Ex 15:1-19). This is what the Church now also chants in the first Hos (praise) of the Midnight Praise ... So the victors here sing a song similar to what Moses uttered.
The song of the Lamb: that is, this praise is offered to Christ the Redeemer as it is to His Father.

As for the content of this praise, it is the confession of the greatness of God's dispensation in all His works, and rejoicing in His infinite power, and that all His commandments, promises and covenants are true, and that He reigns over the hearts of His holy children, that is, those who have consecrated their hearts to Him.

Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name: in their praise they also confess the awesomeness of the person of God and the power of His name. For the gentle, calm, longsuffering God who loves mankind is Himself the God whom Isaiah, when he saw Him in his vision, cried out, saying, "Woe is me, for I am a man of unclean lips" (Isa 6:5). All nations shall come and worship before thee: all people without exception (the wicked and the righteous) will submit to You and worship before You on the day of judgment, and will declare that You alone are worthy of worship and no other (not the beast, to whom the wicked bowed down before). The worship of the wicked is not adoration but fear and terror of the wrath that is coming upon them.

Thy judgments are made manifest: that is, Your justice has been completed and You have proclaimed Your judgments, and what was not understood has become plain and clear, and You have revealed it to us.

The children of God complete their glorification of Him on the day of judgment, proclaiming His holiness and fear, and the submission of all mankind to Him, after the perfection of His mercy toward His children and His justice in the judgment of the wicked has appeared.
And after that: an expression used often, by which St. John moves us from one scene to another.

The tabernacle of the testimony: this is the tabernacle of meeting, and it was given this name because it contained the tablets of the Law, "the testimony." Stephen also used this name (Acts 7:44). St. John saw a vision of the tabernacle of meeting, but in heaven, and its temple signifies the divine presence and will. The going out of the seven angels means that they went out charged with a majestic divine command. The description of what these angels wore agrees with the garments of the priests in the Old Testament, "linen," which signifies purity and cleanness; and they also resemble the splendor of their God, who appeared girt with a golden girdle (ch. 1:13), because He is the one High Priest, and their clothing like what He wears means that they represent Him and carry out His will.

One of the angels who are near to God and always present before Him (one of the four living creatures) gave the seven angels seven bowls, and they are of gold, pointing to the fact that their source is from God and that they represent His justice and His wrath against the wicked.
The bowl: a concave vessel, used for putting incense and offering it during worship.

The temple was filled with smoke: this has no relation to the bowls, for the bowls carried divine wrath, whereas this smoke is one of the manifestations of the glory of God ... as happened when Moses received the tablets of the Law, and the mountain smoked like a furnace (Ex 19:18); likewise at the dedication of the temple in the days of Solomon the same smoke settled on the temple (1 Kgs 8:11), and when Isaiah saw the Lord (Isa 6..). Because of the density of this smoke, that is, the greatness of God's glory and power, no one could look or enter until God's dispensation and decree were fulfilled in carrying out His seven plagues through His angels.
Great is Your glory, O Lord ... who is able to describe it or stand before it!!...

But You have granted us not only to stand but to speak with You and to call You our Father ... So teach us also, my Lord, that the sight of Your most holy glory may not be absent from our eyes, so that we pray to You with reverence and contrition and keep our minds under control before You during prayer ... Forgive us, my God, for we often forget!!! The seven bowls of God's wrath: a general introduction to the chapter: this chapter comes as a continuation of what chapter fifteen indicated (the plagues of the seven angels), and here it describes them in detail. In these seven plagues the following is noted:

First: their resemblance to a great extent to the ten plagues with which God struck the Egyptians, with the difference that they are symbolic and carry spiritual meanings, whereas the ten plagues were, as God spoke them, entirely real.
Second: they also resemble the seven doors, which likewise carried plagues and vengeance, but they are more severe than the plagues of the trumpets (Rev 6-8).
Bowls: plural of bowl, and the bowl is a vessel resembling a cup.

St. John heard the command issued to begin carrying out, that is, to pour out these plagues (the bowls) on the earth. He describes the voice as great, to indicate the severity of the events that follow, and the coming of this voice out of the temple means that it represents the divine will.
And the first went: that is, the first of the angels holding the bowls.
A noisome sore: that is, incurable and unknown to physicians.

After the command was given to the angels, the first carried it out, and his plague covered the earth, but it did not strike all its inhabitants, only those who followed Satan and departed from the way of divine truth. This plague of sores resembles the sixth plague with which God struck the Egyptians, and the resemblance increases in that it did not strike everyone who was in the land of Egypt, but those who bore the mark of "Pharaoh," that is, the idolaters, while the people of God were kept safe from it. The sores point to agitation and anxiety, for their spread over the body takes away its rest; likewise their foul smell points to the blasphemies of the people who have the image of the beast. The most severe thing about this plague is that it is a plague without cure, and how terrible it is for a man to suffer a pain for which there is no healing and no end.

My God, is this not what really happens to everyone who leaves the way and bows down to the beast, that is, gives himself up to the world and its authority and its pleasures, so that the result is anxiety, weariness and pain that has no end except by returning to Your embrace and enjoying Your presence .. I thank You, my God, because to everyone who lives with You You have given immunity from such painful plagues.
This plague reminds us of the plague of the second trumpet, which took a third of the sea only (ch. 8:8), but here, because of its severity, the plague covered the sea and everything in it.
The sea: points to the world, troubled in its thoughts and deeds.
It became blood: the worst sight, which the human soul shrinks from looking at.
As the blood of a dead man: that is, congealed blood that has lost life and the self-movement it carries, and therefore it is clotted and putrid blood.
Every living soul .. died: what is meant is the people whom the world sweeps along in its currents, who bear no spiritual identity and did not respond to God and His calls.

The divine inspiration uses the images most cruel to the soul to depict the state of those upon whom God's wrath comes .. and the first purpose of this hard description is to move people to repentance and return, so that they may have deliverance from these woes.

What happened in the sea also covered all the rivers, which always signify the sources of life, as if God wants to tell us that death will be general, covering everything. This plague reminds us of the first plague with which God struck Pharaoh and the land of Egypt as well (Ex 7:19). Perhaps also the rivers and springs point to the heretics, who were at first a spring of sound teaching and faith, then deviated and began to offer poisoned water and teaching contrary to what the Church received, and for this reason they deserved the bowl of God's wrath.
For they have shed ..: the words here refer to the followers of the beast who bear his mark and persecute the Church of God, or to the heretics who wearied the Church with their heresies.

Because of the difficulty and severity of this plague, the words came on the tongue of the angel, showing that what happened was connected with the absolute justice of God and His eloquence, and the angel's words came in the form of:
1- Praise of the name of God: for he glorified God, the eternal and everlasting One, and highlighted the attribute of His absolute justice in His judgments.

2- A clarification that what happens to the wicked is what they truly deserve, and that the punishment came in the same kind as the wrong (v. 8); and because they shed blood, they were given blood to drink, "for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap" (Gal 6:7).

3- Confession (v. 7:), that is, the rest of the heavenly creation, in the person of the other angel, declared its faith in what the first angel uttered, that God is the true and just One in all His judgments and repays each one according to his deserving, and although He is longsuffering toward the wicked, His punishment remains for the one who does not repent.

My God and good Savior, no sooner do my eyes fall upon the words that speak of Your justice and Your recompense than I find myself trembling, remembering my sins, and nothing rescues me from this except remembering Your very wide mercies toward everyone who seeks them ... and therefore I cry out with all the people of Your Church, "According to Your mercy, O Lord, and not according to our sins."

The sun is supposed to be a source of warmth, light and joy, as it is one of the essentials of life, but it turned into an instrument of burning and severe pain. The meaning intended by this is that everything that was a cause of blessing, pride or comfort .. became a cause of pain and distress. The fire here is figurative, for it is not reasonable that one who was greatly burned should still be alive and blaspheme the name of God. But this applies even more to the material goods that God gives to man, yet because people are immersed in them and preoccupied with them, they turn into a burning, disturbing fire that robs them of their peace and even consumes and devours them, so they forget God; and instead of returning to Him and confessing their sins so that the blessing might return to them, they blaspheme His name and reject Him, and so their gloom and distress increase and they suffer by them.

The fifth divine vengeance came directed at the kingdom of the beast himself, which is every power opposed to the Kingdom of Christ. And because they are the very kingdom of darkness, God's vengeance on them was to strike them with more darkness, so that they become like blind men stumbling about. And to show the severity of their pains from this plague, the inspired text portrays them as "gnawing their tongues," for it is known that biting the tongue is very painful to a person, so how great must the pain be that makes a man bite his tongue?!

Like all the preceding ones, this plague did not bring them to repentance; on the contrary, they went from darkness to the pain of "sores," and from pain to despair, so they blasphemed the name of the Most High God.

I wish, my brother, that you would use the world but not let it rule over you, nor cling to it. Do not give yourself all that you desire, and use everything in measure, even if you have the ability to buy and possess all you want. Here the importance of fasting and keeping to it appears, for it helps you to control yourself so that these desires do not enslave you, and the devil is unable to fight you with them, so that you have deliverance from these plagues that strike the wicked who are immersed in the world.

Babylon was the kingdom of evil that took captive and enslaved the people of God, and it became in the Holy Bible a symbol of all evil and its power. Here the divine wrath came directed at its most famous river (the Euphrates), the cause of its pride and its prosperity, and God dried it up, that is, He confined its glory, pointing to the beginning of its passing away and the end of its iniquity. The kings of the east: after God removed the glory of Babylon by drying up its river (the Euphrates), there come out from God, that is, from the East, kings who reign in place of Babylon, and this is what happened when the kingdom of the Medes and Persians removed the Babylonian empire, and it will happen at the end when Christ reigns after He removes the kingdom of Satan.
It is noted that verses 15-16 depict a parenthetical scene between the sixth bowl and the seventh bowl.

The dragon .. the beast .. the false prophet: these are the three powers that Satan uses, who were mentioned in (ch. 13), but the second beast (ch. 13:11) is renamed here "the false prophet." St. John saw Satan here in a new form that indicates his characteristics all the more, since there came out of the mouths of the three, three unclean spirits in the form of frogs .. Why frogs, then ...?! Only because they represent Satan in the best possible way:
1- Frogs are found in pools and in muddy, miry places (for this is the place and standing of Satan.)
2- The frog is an animal ugly in color and form.
3- The frog is a nocturnal animal whose home and place is always the darkness.
4- The frog is an animal whose voice (its croaking) disturbs and troubles the people who hear it (as Satan does with the children of God.)

These demons go out with signs and wonders that reach the point of miracles, and they know that this is their last war (especially after the river Euphrates has dried up), so they strive to gather all their children, the wicked rulers of this world, to fight the children of God in their last war with them.
That great day: it is the day of God's just and final judgment, that is, the day of judgment.
God Almighty: that is, whatever Satan does, the victory belongs to God alone.
Behold, I come as a thief: the words here are the Lord Christ's, and they mean that He comes suddenly and without any fixed time for His coming.
Keepeth his garments: that is, prepared, wearing the garments of virtue and righteousness.
Lest he walk naked: that is, whoever Christ finds unprepared at the time of His coming will be exposed before people, and they will see his shame.
This verse is parenthetical between verses 15-16, and it is a call from Christ to all His followers to watch and be prepared to meet Him at any time.

Understand, O my soul, that dreadful day, and awake and trim your lamp with the oil of gladness, for you do not know when the voice will come to you saying, Behold, the Bridegroom has come. So take heed, O my soul, do not slumber, lest you stand outside like the five foolish virgins, but watch, entreating, that you may meet Christ the Lord ... and He may grant you the wedding feast of His true divine glory) ... from the prayers of the Agpeya.(
And he gathered them together: that is, Satan with his unclean spirits gathered all his followers and his armies.

Armageddon: a Hebrew word meaning the mountain of Megiddo, a mountain well known to the Jews that witnessed various historical events, such as the victory of the judges Gideon, Barak and Deborah. Since Satan knew that the end of his work on earth was near, he gathered all his energies for the last war. Of course "Armageddon" here does not point to a specific place, for the war is not material, but it points to the final battle and the defeat of Satan and his last judgment.
When the seventh angel poured out the last bowl of God's wrath, heaven declared that the seven bowls were completed.

Into the air: that is, upon the kingdom of Satan, who considered the air his dwelling and his authority (Eph 2:2). It is done: equivalent to the word "It is finished" that the Savior uttered on the Cross, and in agreement with the phrase "for in them is filled up the wrath of God" (Rev 15:1).

The expression "thunders, and lightnings, and an earthquake" is repeated in several places in the Book of Revelation, such as (ch. 8:5), (ch. 11:19), and they all accompanied important events. But here, because the end has drawn near, St. John makes clear that nothing like it or equal to its power had occurred before, nor one like its violence in all the age of mankind since its creation.

The great city: some saw it as Babylon, because it symbolizes evil, and some saw it as Jerusalem, where Christ was crucified, but in its spiritual meaning it is the kingdom of Satan, of which he boasts. Three parts: that is, it collapsed, was scattered and lost its power, and the number three represents perfection, that is, its ruin was complete.

Great Babylon: it signifies here the center of the great city and the place of the throne and seat of Satan.
