The effect of this great earthquake, or of the last cup of God's wrath, was the collapse of the kingdom of evil and the fall of its power, and Satan himself fell, and likewise all his followers fell, that is, the cities of the nations. But Babylon, which signifies the center of evil and the throne of Satan, was mentioned separately, to make clear that God had another purpose concerning her final, doubled punishment, expressed by "the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath," an expression which as a whole means the wrath stored up by God throughout the days (like aged wine) against evil and its kingdom.

This verse is a continuation and clarification of the picture of the violent earthquake, the like of which has not occurred on the earth, for the islands fled away, meaning they were covered with water and disappeared, and the mountains were not found, meaning the dissolution of the elements of the earth and the beginning of the disappearance of its known geographical features.
A great hail: like the plague of hail on the land of Egypt (Ex 9:18-25). It means the falling of snow with frost.
The weight of a talent: about (17.5 kg), and the meaning intended is its great heaviness upon the people.

The perfection of this plague came in that God sent down upon the people hail the like of which the world had not known before in its severity and strength, so that whoever reflects and understands might have an opportunity for repentance. But alas, as happened before, the people blasphemed God instead of offering repentance to Him. This shows the hardness of people's hearts and their ingratitude in the last time.

If tribulation comes upon you, beware of murmuring, and examine yourself lest it be because of your sin and your negligence or failing in your relationship with God, for God allows all things for your good and for the completion of your repentance. And if it is not because of your sin, accept it as a divine dispensation that helps you to cling to Him, and even if you do not understand now, your acceptance of it will cause God to explain it to you afterward, and then you will be able to understand. Babylon the harlot and the beast: a general introduction: the coming three chapters deal with one idea, which is the fall of Babylon and the proclamation of heaven's victory. In chapter seventeen we find a description of wicked Babylon and her relation to the beast, in chapter eighteen a description of her fall, and in chapter nineteen the proclamation of heaven's victory .. Perhaps many ask why Babylon, and what is her story, and what are her symbols?..! So here, dear reader, is some information about Babylon and her story in the Holy Bible ..

1- She was called Babel "because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth" (Gen 11:9), when they wanted to build a tower after the Flood to take shelter in it and to reach heaven. So it is a place that signifies pride and defiance, and it deserved God's punishment.
2- This city was founded by a man named Nimrod (Gen 10:9), whom the Scripture describes as mighty, and he led many to disobey God.
3- This city was famous for the worship of idols and images, and the most famous of its gods was "Marduk," who symbolizes Satan.

4- It was one of the cities to which the people of God were carried captive and which enslaved them for a time, a strong reference to the kingdom of Satan, which fights and takes captive many of the children of God.

5- Just as Jerusalem was a great city because it points to God's dwelling with men, so Babylon also became a great city, as the Book of Revelation described her, because she represents the dwelling of the great Satan in evil, with all his powers and the wicked men who follow him.

In sum, Babylon signifies Satan (the Antichrist) and his kingdom, and likewise signifies the company of the wicked, lovers of the world and its desires and its false and passing wealth, and in every case she signifies the state of constant enmity with God ..
The great whore: a reference to Babylon, the kingdom of evil, and fornication here is a figure for turning away from God and betraying Him by worshiping the world and Satan.

That sitteth upon many waters: an emphasis that Babylon is what is meant here, since it lies on the great river Euphrates (Jer 51:13), and like the words of the Psalm, "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down" (Ps 137:1). The spiritual meaning will be interpreted in (v. 15). One of the seven angels who carried the bowls of God's wrath spoke to St. John, calling him to see the end and judgment of the kingdom of evil and all its followers, who are symbolized by the many waters, and the detailed discussion of this will come in (v. 15).
The kings of the earth: all the leaders and authorities who contributed to, and called their peoples, directly or indirectly, to leave God and His worship.

In a new description of "Babylon," the angel describes her as the adulterous woman who seduced many peoples to spiritual fornication and used every possible means of enticement, so that most of the inhabitants of the earth stagger and fall into evil and blasphemy like drunkards who have lost consciousness and will.
Into the wilderness: a reference to the spiritual poverty and barrenness in which the kingdom of evil lives. Scarlet: a reference to the bloodiness and ferocity of Satan.
Full of names of blasphemy: that is, blasphemy against God, either by attributing God's attributes to himself or by mocking and ridiculing God and His attributes.

The angel took St. John to a new scene in his vision, "he carried me away in the spirit," and he saw a desolate, frightening wilderness, and he saw the kingdom of evil (the woman Babylon) sitting upon the secret of her strength and support, who is Satan, who carries his kingdom, declaring his ferocity through his bloody color and his hatred of God through his blasphemy and his insolence against His holy name.
Seven heads and ten horns: this was explained before in (ch. 12:3, ch. 13:1), and it points to the multitude of his thoughts and their strength.
Purple: a red color worn by kings in ancient times, and it is like the robe that the Roman soldiers put on the Lord Christ in mockery of Him.
Scarlet: a blood-red color.

In arrogance and pride, Babylon the harlot took on the appearance of kings to proclaim her greatness and authority, so she dresses like them and boasts of her scarlet color because she shed the blood of many saints and drank of their blood, and adorned herself with the vices and sins that her followers desired, such as gold, pearls and precious stones, and she held in her hand a cup of the wine of her pleasure, by which she is refreshed and delights and becomes drunk. And pointing to the intensity of her evil, God declares to us that the content of this cup is fornication and the abominations from which she gives the nations and peoples to drink, and for this it is called "the wine of her fornication" (v. 2). It is also noted that the description of Babylon in this form agrees exactly with her description as given by Jeremiah in (Jer 51:7).
Mystery: that is, the name Babylon here is a symbol, and the discussion is not about the real city of Babylon.
Mother of harlots: the origin of all evil and immorality.

The impudence and boldness of Babylon in her evil reached the point that she was not ashamed of her shameful sin, but boasted of what she commits and advertised herself, with the shamelessness of fornicators in announcing their name and profession to attract others and ensnare them, for she put her name on her forehead. And her description as the origin of all sin, "the mother of harlots," is because she is the caller and instigator of every kind of spiritual fornication and betrayal of the holy name of God and blasphemy against it.

To complete the scene, the woman was in a state of drunken intoxication, and the secret of the happiness and intoxication of her drunkenness is that she was satisfied, and is still being satisfied (the kingdom of evil), with the blood of the faithful children of God who rejected her and resisted her, so she raised persecution and torment against them, and they did not submit or surrender but gave their lives even to death, and therefore their name became great, for they were called "the martyrs of Jesus."

And when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration: that is, I was bewildered and found no explanation, and this wonder is considered an introduction to what the angel will make clear to John in the coming verses.

In the Law of Moses, the priest in ancient times used to put on his forehead a small plate on which was written "Holiness to the LORD," that is, set apart for the service of God; this was a clear declaration of his identity and belonging. Likewise the wicked put their evil name on their foreheads, to declare also their belonging to the satanic kingdom of Babylon, and many people do not know what they are putting on their foreheads, "set apart for the Lord, or living in Babylon..." Have you settled your matter, my brother, and do you know what title you are wearing and to which kingdom you belong ...?!

entries.section: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

paragraphs.text: St. John's wonder at the preceding scene carried more distress than wonder, at God's allowing the woman (Babylon) to delight in and be drunk with the blood of the martyrs, the children of God. So the angel's words to him, "Wherefore didst thou marvel?" came as an introduction to revealing the mystery he was about to declare to St. John.
The beast that thou sawest: it is the beast from the sea mentioned in (Rev 13:1-3), which is one of the forms of Satan.
Was, and is not: a clear reference to the shrinking of the authority of Satan and his kingdom.

Shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition: that is, on the day of the Lord's great judgment he will be moved from the place where the wicked wait to eternal perdition in the abyss forever.

The general meaning is that the beast carrying the woman is none other than Satan, who had authority over man, but by the crucifixion of Christ and His redemption of all mankind, this Satan was driven back, as the Lord Christ said to His disciples, "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. Behold, I give unto you power) "... (Lk 10:17-19), like the words of the Apostle Paul, "And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Col 2:
14-15.) (It appears from this verse that Satan dwells in hell and continues to fight mankind within the limits that God permits him, until he is cast with all his armies into eternal torment.
They that dwell on the earth shall wonder: that is, his followers who bear his mark and sign.
Whose names were not written .. in the book of life: that is, there is no deliverance through him, and it is the natural result for whoever follows him.

The angel adds in his speech to what preceded that the followers of Satan or the Antichrist will be seized with amazement and regret over the one in whom they put their hope to no use or profit, for their fate has become clear: it is perdition and the loss of the inheritance of the Kingdom, "the book of life."
Was, and is not: the wicked realize that the authority of Satan, with which he used to fight the children of God in the world, has ended.
And yet is: although Satan exists in eternal torment, he is unable to do anything.

entries.section: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

paragraphs.text: "Here is the mind which hath wisdom" is a parenthetical sentence whose purpose is to urge the reader or listener to concentrate on what is coming.

The seven heads .. seven mountains: many interpreters held that the scene here is a figure for Rome in its harsh persecution of Christianity, since Rome is in fact built on seven hills. On which the woman sitteth: that is, she exercised her authority and persecution through this city.

entries.section: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

paragraphs.text: Seven kings: many interpreters have labored to say who these seven are, but in keeping with the symbols of the whole book, we see that the number seven here signifies the perfection of the days of the kingdom of evil and Satan throughout history, without being bound to a specific time.
Five are fallen: that is, most of them have gone and their days have passed.
And one is: that is, at the time this book was written.
And the other is not yet come: a prophecy of the coming of a final kingdom of evil before the end of days.

In this verse the vision shows us the succession of the kingdoms of evil to the end of days, for the first five kingdoms are those that opposed God and His people with their idols and wars, and they are the kingdoms of:
1- Egypt, which enslaved the people of God.
2- Assyria, which lifted up its eyes against the Holy One of Israel (Isa 37:23).
3- Babylon, which subdued the whole earth (Jer 50:23).
4- Persia, about which Daniel prophesied (Dan 10:13).
5- Greece, the last pagan error, which defiled Jerusalem and which the Maccabees resisted.

As for the kingdom existing at the time the book was written, it is the Roman kingdom, the sixth, which made Christianity taste the worst kinds of torture and cruelty .. And there remains a final kingdom, the kingdom of the Antichrist, of whom the angel indicates that he must continue a short space, that is, his kingdom and his wars will continue for a short period of time.

entries.section: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

paragraphs.text: The beast that was: that is, Satan (v. 8). Is the eighth: that is, the last of all evil ...

It is clear that the kingdoms are seven and not eight, but the declaration that Satan is the eighth means Satan's domination of all the preceding kingdoms, as if all of them bore his mark, and to show that there is no eighth kingdom the angel declares that his spirit (Satan) is at work and active in the seven kingdoms. And in an ending reassuring to the children of God and in a plain declaration, the angel confirms for the second time, to us and to St. John, the final fate of Satan, which is eternal perdition.

entries.section: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

paragraphs.text: In an interpretation of the scene of the ten horns (v. 3), the angel makes clear in his speech that it is a symbol of ten kingdoms or ten kings (heads of nations) to whom Satan gives authority, but in their evil they are not as strong as the preceding kingdoms, since they receive authority "one hour," that is, a small authority, although they will devote all their power, thought and authority to the service of Satan.

entries.section: (2) The interpretation of the preceding vision

paragraphs.text: These authorities or kingdoms or governments declare their clear defiance of the Lord Jesus, "the slain Lamb," so they fight Him and resist the authority of His Kingdom over the hearts of men ..., and the angel declares to us the final result of this war, which is the defeat of Satan and all his followers, and the proclamation of the victory of Christ, King of kings and Lord of lords, who will lead in the procession of His triumph all His chosen children, those called and those who believe in His name (2 Cor 2:14).

I thank You, my God, that You announce to us our victory in Your blessed name, so that our confidence in our salvation through You is renewed, and our triumph over Satan by the power of Your blessed name and the sign of Your life-giving Cross. I thank You and ask You, my Savior, to complete Your work in me to the end, so that I may not be disturbed by the wars of Satan, and may complete my striving in peace because You are with me.
The waters which thou sawest: they are the same waters he mentioned in (v. 1), but here he will explain them.

The angel brings St. John back to the beginning of the scene he saw in this chapter and explains to him some of its symbols. The woman (Babylon) was sitting, that is, she controls and rules with her evil the peoples of the world of every race and language.

The events of these two verses came in a way none of us expects; for the woman was sitting upon the beast, that is, he was serving her and devoting his power to her ... But let us see what happens! Satan turned against his own kingdom, and there came anger, destruction and killing, and Satan himself began to burn his kingdom and his followers, pointing to the nearness of his end and his final disappearance, for any kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation (Lk 11:17). And before St. John asks how this happens?...! the angel intervenes and reveals to us the secret of what happened, which is that "God hath put in their hearts," that is, this is God's command and His effective will even over the kingdom of evil with all its powers and systems, for the first counsel and the last word belong to Him alone, however patient and longsuffering He is toward the kingdom of evil. And give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God shall be fulfilled: that is, all the authorities and powers and kingdoms gave all their strength and resources to the service of Satan to destroy Babylon, the kingdom of evil. To clarify the idea with examples that bring home to our minds how this happens, we say that God often used some kingdoms of evil to take vengeance on wicked kingdoms that preceded them: the Greeks came against the Persians and the Assyrians, and the Romans came against the Greeks, and so the kingdoms of evil (the beast) rose against one another (Babylon) until they destroyed her and all her authority.

And the woman which thou sawest: that is, the woman who is the subject of the discussion in the whole chapter, who sat upon the beast and upon the many waters (v. 1). At the end of the chapter the angel sums up for us the character of the woman, saying that she is "that great city," that is, the capital of evil in different ages: once (Babylon), which humbled the people of God in ancient times; another time Rome, which made the Christians taste the severest degrees of torment; and a third time, the forces of evil and atheism in the contemporary world; and at every time most of the kings and rulers of the earth submitted to her and followed what she commanded them.

My God, You leave evil to rage against Your children from time to time, and we wonder, why, Lord, are they increased that trouble us!?! But we thank You, my God, that You announce to us and teach us that all this is only for a time, and we must trust in Your wisdom and Your ordering of the times. What You announce to us now brings rest to our souls and shows us all the more the folly of Satan, who has become without wisdom and without authority over his actions, for in the end he finishes himself by himself, like a madman, a fool who thought himself wise..!!! Let us praise Your holy name and thank Your exalted wisdom now and at all times .. Amen.

The destruction of Babylon: introduction: after the previous chapter highlighted how evil was divided against itself, and pointed to the collapse of its kingdom (Babylon), this chapter portrays for us a detailed picture of the fall of Babylon, the reason for her fall, and the weeping of the wicked over her. We also find God's clear call to His children to come out of her, lest the final plagues fall upon them.

entries.section: (1) The proclamation of the first angel

paragraphs.text: And after these things: that is, the preceding vision of the beast and the harlot (ch. 17). The earth was lightened with his glory: a figure for the power, the greatness of authority and the majesty of this angel.

In a scene considered a continuation of what John saw in the preceding chapter, here he saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, making a proclamation long awaited by the faithful children of God, and because of the power of this angel his descent from heaven was accompanied by a great light that lit up the whole earth.

entries.section: (1) The proclamation of the first angel

paragraphs.text: Hold: a prison.

The angel proclaimed with a loud voice (a cry) the subject of the message he carries to all the inhabitants of the earth, which is the fall of the kingdom of evil (Babylon), and he repeated the word "fallen" to indicate her final fall, with no rising again or return of her authority, and he adds that she has become a prison for all the demons and unclean spirits and also every unclean bird.

An unclean bird: there were kinds of birds that God forbade the Jewish people to eat in the Law, such as birds of prey, and they were hated birds among the people ... But the meaning here is another description of the demons, besides his first description of them as unclean spirits.

entries.section: (1) The proclamation of the first angel

paragraphs.text: This verse makes clear to us the reasons for the fall of Babylon and her just judgment, for she:

(1) Made all her followers drunk by offering various desires (the wine of her fornication), so these services and desires were the cause of their fornication (that is, turning away from God.) (2) And as she destroyed nations and peoples, so she also brought down many kings and rulers by various tricks to ensure her dominion over the whole world.
(3) By enticements and material gains she was able to control the merchants of the earth (the economic powers), so that they worship money and its power instead of God.

Very comforting, Lord, is the meditation on the judgments of Your justice, for You announce to us how the kingdom of evil ends and becomes a dwelling and a prison for Satan and his unclean spirits; but I, my God, look with longing to the other dwelling, where You are there, a shining light and warmth and tenderness and rest without end, and until we meet You there and enjoy the sight of You, I pray to You and ask You to complete for us the way of our salvation and to rescue us from the earthly (Babylon) with all her evil desires and pleasures.

entries.section: (2) The warning of the second angel

paragraphs.text: St. John heard a second voice, also from heaven, and this voice carried a warning from God to His people, calling them to come out of Babylon before He brings His punishment upon her; and the spiritual meaning here is that God calls us and urges us to depart from evil finally, for spiritual Babylon is not a particular place but a state present now everywhere, but the faithful children of God must flee from every form of evil.

That ye be not partakers of her sins: this is the reason for God's call to us to withdraw from evil, because it is impossible for a person to live inside the kingdom of evil without being affected by it or by its enticements ... This also reminds us of the angel's call to Lot to flee from Sodom and Gomorrah (wicked Babylon) before their destruction and burning (Gen 19).

entries.section: (2) The warning of the second angel

paragraphs.text: Her sins have reached unto heaven: a pictorial expression indicating the severity of her evil. As the inspired text also describes that the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah had reached the Lord (Gen 18:20). God hath remembered her iniquities: this does not of course mean that God had forgotten, but that the time of punishment and judgment has come.

entries.section: (2) The warning of the second angel

paragraphs.text: After God commanded His people and those who love Him to come out of Babylon and withdraw from evil, His direct command to repay her comes. This command is of course directed to God's servants, the angels who carry out His will, and we notice about God's repayment that it is:
(1) Just: "Reward her even as she rewarded you," that is, as she tormented the children of God with many torments.

(2) Doubled: "Double unto her double," that is, she will suffer as no one has ever imagined or thought, and as she mixed desires and enticements in the cup of her fornication, it is now her turn to drink from the same cup, but here she drinks a doubled mixture of the wrath of God.

entries.section: (2) The warning of the second angel

paragraphs.text: She hath glorified herself: the characteristic of Satan and of evil is pride and boasting.
Lived deliciously: in earthly and sensual pleasures and sinful, passing desires.
I am no widow: I am not in want or need and I will not see old age or an end.

In pride and haughtiness Babylon looked upon the glories of her evil, and in stupidity and pride she did not suppose for a moment that all this has a certain end, so the voice of her boasting rose and she declared that she is a queen and a young woman living in luxury and there is no passing away of her glory or her false happiness..; and for this God's sentence came that she should pay the price of her stubbornness and unrepentance, so in proportion to her fornication and evil she will also receive her portion of torment and sorrow and wailing and gnashing of teeth.

entries.section: (2) The warning of the second angel

paragraphs.text: In a proclamation that reassures the children of God by the power of their heavenly Father and the might of His right hand, saving to His children and destroying to those who oppose and resist Him, he tells us how the day of God's vengeance will be.

In one day: that is, the plagues come in succession and with speed, and the day is a reference to the day of the last judgment; and these plagues begin with death, that is, the proclamation of the destruction of all her inhabitants and her kings, and mourning and famine are two punishments that correspond to the glory and luxury (v. 7) by which she deceived and seduced her children, and the fire that burns her is the punishment of her fornication that awaits her, as the Law commanded in the punishment of fornicators (Lev 20:14, 21:9). The meaning intended by death here may be the end of the whole world, and consequently her eternal fate (Babylon's) is perpetual mourning and a hunger for the rest that the wicked do not find, and then burning with a fire that is not quenched.

Beloved, do not be amazed if you see the boasting and prosperity of the wicked and the success of their ways ... and be assured that they have a short time, but after this they pay the price of their luxury. So reject evil and all its desires strongly, for in proportion as you flee from (Babylon), as Joseph fled from the offers and enticements of sin, we will have deliverance in the name of our Savior Christ and the inheritance of His eternal throne.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: The kings of the earth: an expression that points to the proud and haughty, to whom evil gave authority and worldly influence (leaders or politicians). Lived deliciously with her: they satisfied their evil desires through her (the kingdom of evil). Everyone who had any standing stood, and their hopes were disappointed and ended as they saw their kingdom collapsing before their eyes into destruction, and her eternal judgment and harsh torment had begun. And because her torment and judgment is a declaration of their own end and judgment too, their weeping, mourning and crying came not only over the city but also over themselves, since their fate had become before them, and for this they uttered the expression "Alas, alas," to declare their anguish at what has come upon her and their terror at what awaits them.

Standing afar off: it may be a picture showing a time difference between the judgment of the kingdom of evil (Babylon) and then of her followers (the kings of the earth), and it is an expression that points to the severest kinds of torment, for how cruel it is for a person to see the judgment and torment of another while knowing that he is seeing what will happen to himself also.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: The second kind are "the merchants of the earth"; if the first kind were attracted by authority, influence and rule, there are also those whom love of money and gold enslaved, and whom the world attracted with its business and deals, and all their hope was in increasing their money and leaving it as an inheritance to their children. What they weep over now is their discovery of the deception into which they fell and that all they did is worthless, "no man buyeth their merchandise any more," and of course their mourning is also over the torment and judgment that await them, which have become present before them, as was the feeling of the kings of the earth.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: Fine linen: delicate linen.
Purple: luxurious red cloth.
Scarlet: red cloth darker than purple.
Thyine wood: fragrant wood from the citron tree found in North Africa.
Marble: one of the finest kinds of marble.
Fine flour: choice flour.
Wheat: grain.
Odours: sweet perfumes.

These two verses make clear the kinds of trade of these merchants, which included everything, beginning with precious riches (such as gold, silver, pearls and precious stone), then the most splendid garments (purple, scarlet and fine linen), followed by what ordinary people need in their homes (ivory, wood and iron) to furnish their houses, and what everyone needs for eating (such as oil, wheat and the flesh of cattle), then the end was with the worst kind of trade, which is trade in people themselves and their bodies (the trade of fornication...). The purpose of presenting all these kinds of goods to the merchants is to expose what is happening in the world now, for the merchants, the followers of (Babylon) and the kingdom of evil, made it lawful to trade in everything, the lawful and the unlawful, and the purpose was to exploit people to make their gain and to entice them constantly to buy, so that man remains all his life a captive of his desires and ambitions and material needs; on the one hand the wealth of the merchants of evil increases, and on the other hand people forget the salvation of their souls in their rush to buy.

In a more spiritual way it can be said that the merchants here are the demons and the goods are the enticements and desires, and their variety means that Satan offers each person what entices him, whether it is clear evil (people's bodies) or hidden sins that he persuades people they badly need (such as adornment, clothing and desires for food), so he ties all people with threads whose end is in his hand, and controls the whole world by this trade of his.

I thank You, my God, that You expose to me the plans of the merchants of evil. So understand, O my soul, and be chaste, and do not ask for more than you need, and be content with what you have, lest you lose your authority over yourself and give it to Satan, for in the end he will give you to taste nothing but the husks of the swine, that is, humiliation and misery.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: Fruits: produce.
Fat: precious.
The words here in their direct meaning refer to (Babylon), who lost everything, and also her merchants, who lost their trade with her burning.

As for the spiritual meaning, it can be applied to every soul that went after its desires and thereby lost the fruit of the Holy Spirit expected of it, and the radiant Christ departed from it and it will not find Him afterward, since it left Him first, so He left it finally and deprived it of its eternal inheritance.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: These two verses correspond in their meaning and picture with what is said in (vv. 9, 10) about the kings of the earth, for the merchants also shared in the mourning, weeping, lamentation and great fear, not only over the passing splendor of the kingdom of evil but also over the torment that awaits them.
Clothed in fine linen .. arrayed in fine linen: that is, she who once had splendor. Shipmasters: the captains of ships.
Sailors: those who keep the sea charts and guide the ships.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: The words here are about the third group (the shipmasters and sailors at sea) after the kings of the earth and her merchants, and this third group signifies the middlemen of evil, that is, those who transport it from one place to another and promote it or import strange sins and re-export them, and the Lord Christ Himself cursed them when He said, "Woe unto that man by whom the offence cometh!" (Mt 18:7). They too cried out when they saw the collapse and burning of the city of their harbor, and they never believed in her end, for they thought she was great and above all destruction.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: Dust on their heads: an ancient custom of the Eastern peoples to show intense grief.

The shipmasters and sailors repeated almost what the kings and merchants had repeated before, as their hopes collapsed and were ruined with the end and destruction of Babylon, for after having been the cause of their wealth she has now become desolate before their eyes. And their cry, as we explained before, is their fear of their coming fate.

entries.section: (3) The grief and lament of her followers

paragraphs.text: Rejoice: this is a call from the same angel who proclaimed the judgment of Babylon, for he also proclaims the joy of the kingdom of heaven.

The angel declares to the heavenly creation and all the martyrs good news, which is the end of Babylon and the beginning of her judgment and the proclamation of divine justice, and the expression that "God hath avenged you on her" is an answer to the question that the holy martyrs asked: "How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood" (Rev 6:10). And so, just as God's mercies gladden heaven and the saints by the acceptance of the penitent, so also His justice in repaying the wicked gladdens all heaven, because it is a victory for the truth and not a gloating over the wicked.

entries.section: (4) The confirmation of the fall of evil (Babylon)

paragraphs.text: A stone like a great millstone: a millstone is a heavy stone used in grinding wheat.

After this St. John saw an angel whom he described as "mighty," pointing to the greatness of the work he was about to do, for he took up a large round stone and cast it into the sea, so that it sank quickly because of its great weight, then he declared afterward that what he did with the stone is a representation of what will be done to great Babylon in her strength and weight, that is, her end and her disappearance from the face of the earth forever.

entries.section: (4) The confirmation of the fall of evil (Babylon)

paragraphs.text: In these two verses he confirms the features of the death and final end of the city of evil, making clear the end of everything in it that carries marks of life or joy or movement .. There will be no more in her one who sings with his voice or strikes and plays the instruments of joyful music, such as the harp (the stringed instrument) or the pipe (the wind instrument). And what happened to the makers of entertainment happens also to every industry, even the necessary ones such as preparing the flour that would be used as bread for her, that is, she will lose even necessary food and die.

And as her works will end, her entertainment will be quenched, every light in her, and light is usually linked with glory, so her passing away means the passing and end of the glory of the kingdom of evil, of which she boasted for a time .. and likewise there will be no joys in you at all, "the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride."

And in the end the angel repeats to us what has been announced many times, that the reason for her destruction is God's just vengeance on her merchants (v. 11), who supplied her with every kind of evil and facilitated the seduction of the whole earth, and likewise her sorcery, which attracted and led astray most of the peoples.

entries.section: (4) The confirmation of the fall of evil (Babylon)

paragraphs.text: This verse adds another reason for the carrying out of God's just punishment and the destruction of Babylon, which is her shedding of the blood of His children the prophets and the saints and all those she killed among the inhabitants of the earth, whether by persecuting them or by seducing them.

Truly the end of evil is painful and shameful and there is no escape from it .. Here is the end for everyone who neglected and made light of God's successive warnings .. So we must repent every day, even if with a few words, lest the heedlessness of life take us and (Babylon) with her sorcery and enticements make us fall, so that we sink with her in the sea of the judgment of perdition and lose our eternal life.
The joys of heaven's victory
"Alleluia": an expression meaning joy and rejoicing, and it also carries praise and glorification.
A great multitude: an expression of the large number, and also the variety of groups.

After that St. John heard a voice coming from all the heavenly creation (angels and the spirits of the martyrs and saints) declaring their joy, and they rejoiced with thanksgiving, praising God, and the words of their praise carried and made clear the reasons for this joy.

The first reason is the greatness of the Lord the Savior and the greatness of His salvation, for He alone is the owner of glory and honor and is almighty, and this is what the Church repeats in the prayers of the Pascha Week when she prays: "Yours is the power, the glory, the blessing and the majesty forever."

The second reason is the joy that God's judgments are just judgments, and even if He delays in them, the condemnation of evil gladdens everyone who lived and strove in righteousness and godliness, especially when they see the condemnation of the kingdom of evil and its head, Satan, and their being tormented just as they also tormented His holy children. And just as the bliss that the faithful children of God will enjoy is eternal, so also the torment of the kingdom of evil will be eternal, for the smoke of her burning rises up forever and ever.

After St. John gathered all the heavenly creation in the scene of praise and rejoicing, he draws closer to the throne of God, where the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures surrounding the throne of God (see ch. 4:4-8) repeat the scene of worship and cry out like the cry of the heavenly multitude, "Amen; Alleluia," confirming their sharing with the multitude in joy and praise.
Came out of the throne: we do not know whose this voice is, but it came out from the center of heaven, that is, the throne of God.

Ye that fear him: those who lived in the fear of God, and this fear kept them from the kingdom of evil. Both small and great: that is, whatever the stature or rank, the call to praise is general for everyone. A call came from one of the heavenly creatures declaring that everyone must share in praise, singing and gladness and in confessing the work of God and His justice.

The whole heavenly creation responded to the call by offering praise and glory to God, and because of the intensity and greatness of its voice it is described as "the voice of a great multitude," like the sound of the falling waters of mighty waterfalls and like the sound of thunder terrifying in people's ears. As for the subject and words of its praise, it was the proclamation of the complete Kingdom of God and His absolute sovereignty over everything after the end and passing away of the kingdom of evil, and in this they present to us a third reason for the song of joy.
The marriage of the Lamb: the proclamation of the Kingdom of God at His Second Coming.
His wife: His striving Church, for whom the time of her joy and the proclamation of her victory has come.

A fourth reason for the joys of heaven, which is the proclamation of the beginning of the joys of the marriage of the Lamb, when He comes in His Second Coming and announces the end of life on earth and the beginning of eternal life and happiness. The phrase "the marriage of the Lamb" means that it is a joy whose center and source is Christ Himself, while His wife is a symbol of the faithful, striving Church that endured terrors and whose time of delight has at last come... The meaning also includes Christ's eternal union (expressed by marriage) with each individual human soul that kept its purity and was not defiled by the world and never made Babylon its home, and for this its reward is to put on the dress of the bride and appear in her most splendid adornment.

Her adornment and purity is expressed by the pure linen (fine linen), which points to her purity, cleanness and righteousness (the Church or the soul), for it is known that nothing unclean will enter heaven (Rev 21:8), and the expression "was granted" means that Christ in His justice and vengeance on Satan and his kingdom and followers also rewards those of His holy children who were faithful, since He alone is the source of every gift, joy, grace and eternal happiness.

My Lord and beloved God, meditation and gazing on this beautiful and wonderful scene creates in the soul longings and eagerness that make it understand the feelings of St. Paul when he declared the desire of his heart and his wish to depart from earth to heaven, where the marriage of the Lamb is. But these longings, my Lord, often wither in the heart and I forget them.. So I beg You, my Lord, do not allow the world and all its concerns to take these feelings from my heart, but always renew my longing for You and for the splendor of the glory of Your heavenly wedding... that no one may take my crown.

entries.section: (2) The blessedness and happiness of the saints

paragraphs.text: The angel commanded St. John to write, a command that has been repeated many times, and the purpose of repeating the command is to highlight the importance of what is coming. What God wanted written and to reach us is a message of encouragement to urge us to continue the spiritual striving to the end. First he declares the happiness of the faithful strivers who have been given (the invitation) to enter the glories of the Kingdom, and second he affirms that this will happen and is certain, for the words and promises of God are true and sure.

entries.section: (2) The blessedness and happiness of the saints

paragraphs.text: Before the awe of the situation and the joy of the good news he had heard, St. John found himself prostrating in humility before the angel, who forbade him, since he (the angel) is also one of God's creatures and servants, and worship should be to God alone.
That have the testimony of Jesus: an expression that refers to the earthly creation and its duty of witness, preaching and praise to the Lord Jesus.

The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy: that is, witness and preaching in the name of the Lord Christ is the foundation of all prophecy, for the aim of the prophecies of the prophets in the Old Testament was the coming Christ, and in the New Testament the word prophecy means more teaching, because it speaks of the coming Kingdom of God, and every teaching in the New Testament has Christ as its aim.

A note: "worship God": some exploit this verse and attack the tradition of the Coptic people of bowing before the Father bishops and kissing their hands..; but the firm and most beautiful teaching in the Church is that the submission and bowing is not to the person of the man himself (for we do not worship anyone but God) but we believe that we bow to the grace and gift of the priesthood (the priesthood of Christ Himself), which was handed over through Christ to the Apostles, and from them to the Father bishops by the holy breathing (Jn 20:22). The meaning, simply, is that we worship Christ who is hidden in the glory of His priesthood. In addition, all people agree that bowing is respect for those of standing in all the world.

I wish, my brother, that you would remember the Kingdom with all its joys, so that you leave behind the passing pleasures of sin and also make light of the temporary pains of life, and strive diligently with fervent worship and the labors of service by which you express your love for God and for all around you.

entries.section: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

paragraphs.text: St. John describes a new scene for us, as he sees the Lord Christ sitting on a white horse, the same sight he saw at the opening of the first seal (ch. 6:2), and this vision makes clear to us some of the attributes of the Lord Christ:
a) Power: for He is a warrior horseman who went out to conquer (ch. 6). b) Purity and cleanness: for the color white is always a symbol of purity and cleanness.
c) Faithful and True: faithful in completing His redemption and proclaiming His victory, and true in His promises and covenants to His children and those who love Him.
d) Just: for He judges in justice and gives each one according to his work.
e) Supporting: for He fights with His children and for them against all the schemes of the evil enemy.

entries.section: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

paragraphs.text: His eyes were as a flame of fire: that is, the Searcher of hidden things; see also (ch. 1:14, ch. 2:18). On his head were many crowns: every king and kingdom has one crown, but the many crowns are a figure for His absolute authority over all creation and the nations, for He is King of kings.
He had a name written, that no man knew: because His name is the essence of God Himself, unlimited and incomprehensible to man.

St. John continues the description of the Lord Christ, declaring to us the power of His eyes, from which nothing hides or is hidden, and the authority of His absolute kingship over all, and also pointing to His wonderful and glorious name, whose dimensions no one grasps, and this reminds us of Moses' meeting with God (Ex 3:13, 14) when he asked about His name and God answered him "I AM THAT I AM," that is, the One who is and who will be, and there is no single name that expresses His divine essence (see also Isa 9:6), where Isaiah prophesied about the birth of Christ and described His name as wonderful.

entries.section: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

paragraphs.text: Clothed with a vesture: wearing a garment like the garments of the priests; see the explanation of (ch. 1:13). The scene that St. John sees here is very similar to what he saw at the beginning of the Book of Revelation (ch. 1), but he adds to it that the garment of His priesthood is dipped in blood, and the meaning here is very clear, for he sees the Lord Christ the High Priest (Heb 4:14) and sees Him also as a sacrifice of redemption offered for us all, so He is the sacrifice and He is also the priest who offered it.
His name is The Word of God: and it is the divine name of the Lord Christ or His hypostatic name (Jn 1:1). This was explained in detail in the commentary on the Gospel of John.

entries.section: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

paragraphs.text: The armies: the name of armies or heavenly hosts has been associated with the angels, but there is nothing here to prevent the multitudes of the saints from being with them also.
Fine linen, white: white linen.

As the Lord Christ went out on a white horse, He also gave by His grace to all who completed their striving and overcame to go out and follow Him in the procession of His victory, riding white horses like Him, as if He makes them partners with Him in the glories of His victory, and He clothed them in white linen, a symbol of the purity of their conduct and their cleanness by which and for which they lived.

entries.section: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

paragraphs.text: A sharp sword: that is, His word or His speech; see (ch. 1:16). With it he should smite the nations: a figure for the severity of His word by which He will judge the nations.

A rod of iron: that is, His strong authority over His enemies; see also (ch. 12:5). The winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God: an expression used to highlight the power of God's vengeance on evil and the wicked and His unlimited ability; see also (ch. 14:20). St. John continues describing the scene of his vision of Christ, making clear to us the power of His word, which will judge the wicked since they did not act on it and did not turn back from their evil, so His word becomes a judgment on them, as the Lord Christ Himself said, "the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day" (Jn 12:48), and likewise He will have the authority of a king over them (the rod) since the time of their repayment has come. And to highlight the intensity of the wrath and vengeance, St. John goes on and reminds us of the scene of "the winepress," for the Romans used to make stone basins dug in the ground and put grapes in them, and some slaves would go down barefoot to tread the grapes with their feet to press them as a first step in preparing wine, so likewise the enemies of God become like trodden grapes.

entries.section: (3) The scene of the triumphant Christ

paragraphs.text: In (v. 12) St. John mentioned that the name of God is great and no one knows its dimensions, but here he mentions that God, that is, the Lord Christ, is clothed with His name "on his vesture," and the meaning is that the greatness of the name of God covers the whole world. As for the name being written on the thigh, this is a reference to the power and the continuous divine work in saving His children and refuting evil; and the name declared to us here, "King of kings and Lord of lords," makes clear to us that the glory of God and His Kingdom has no likeness in any of the great kingdoms of the world that people have known, indeed in truth there is not the slightest comparison, for Christ alone is the Lord of all creation and its King, whether this creation is heavenly or earthly.
The words can also be interpreted symbolically, considering that His garment signifies His Church, which proclaims His name before the whole world for repentance and the acceptance of salvation.

Let us ask ourselves every day before we sleep .. was Christ truly my King and my Lord all day long .. or did I, without meaning to, have another king and lord from the material things of the world .. My God, I want You alone to be my only King, but I often go astray, so I beg You, my God, help me to consecrate my whole heart to You alone and desire nothing but Your Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) The scene of the end of evil

paragraphs.text: St. John continues his vision of the scene of the last victory, declaring the appearance of an angel standing in the sun, that is, visible to all, and he cried with a loud voice because of the importance of what he would proclaim to all. He called to all the fowls of heaven, meaning the birds of prey that eat flesh, for God has prepared for them a great supper from the remains of the members of the kingdom of evil who were trodden down (v. 15), for these birds to eat them.. and he mentioned in the explanation of (v. 18) these members, for they were the kings of evil, its commanders, its mighty men and its horsemen, and the birds ate their flesh, from the greatest of them to the smallest, and the scene as a whole is a completion of the picture of God's wrath and vengeance on the wicked.

A note: many of the Fathers reflected on the difference between the scene of the "marriage supper" (v. 9), which is for those who love the holy name of God, that joyful supper, and this supper, great in its ruin and calamity for the wicked.

entries.section: (4) The scene of the end of evil

paragraphs.text: In a last scene representing the last desperate attempt made by the beast, the representative of Satan and his fiercest commander (ch. 13:1), as he gathers all his wicked followers to make a final war against Christ after the proclamation of their judgment and destruction, the final end comes and the Lord Christ seizes the beast and his representative the Antichrist, who led the nations astray by the wonders he performed (see ch. 13:11-17) until they went whoring after him and left God.

Them that had received the mark of the beast: that is, those who followed Satan and accepted him as their god instead of God (see ch. 13:15, ch. 14:11). Both were cast: that is, the beast and the false prophet.
Alive: a figure for the severity of the torment, for how cruel it is for something living to be burned.

A lake of fire burning with brimstone: a figure for the breadth of the circle of the fire, "lake," and its intensity, "brimstone," and it will be mentioned also in (ch. 20, 21), and it is a reference to eternal judgment and endless torment, and it is not hell, that is, the temporary place where the wicked await judgment.

A note: if the name of the beast is mentioned alone, it is a symbolic indication of the kingdom of Satan and his mark, and if the name of the dragon is mentioned with it, the dragon is the great Satan and the beast is his greatest commander, and with them the false prophet (ch. 13:2, ch. 16:13).

entries.section: (4) The scene of the end of evil

paragraphs.text: The remnant: that is, the earthly kings and leaders of evil other than the beast and the Antichrist, whose judgment was completed.
Slain with the sword of him that sat: that is, their judgment was carried out by the judgments of His word.
All the fowls were filled: a figure for the end of evil and the completion of God's just judgment.

In reference to the scene of judgment, all the wicked will stand before God and be tried and condemned before His word and His commandment that they neglected and squandered, so it will be like the sword that first bears witness to their transgression and then leads them to destruction, so that they become a meal for the birds of prey of heaven, in a painful and terrifying scene and a certain fate for everyone who neglected God's successive warnings (v. 17).

Do not persist in your sin like Satan and all his wicked followers, who await eternal torment. You are different from him because you are a child of God, and however great your fall may be, return to Him quickly and He will embrace you and forgive you and support you with His power and adorn you with His virtues. Remembering the judgment keeps you away from many desires and from negligence and laziness, and you win the salvation of your soul.

The binding of Satan, his loosing, and the thousand-year reign: introduction to the chapter: this chapter is considered one of the very important parts of the Book of Revelation, since it deals with the subject of "the reign of Christ for a thousand years.." which has led some to actually await the Second Coming of Christ to reign on earth. Of course the Church rejects this direction in interpretation; for the book as a whole is a spiritual book and all its meanings are symbolic, and many, indeed all, of the numbers and figures that come in it have no relation to earthly time in its days and hours by which we work now.

entries.section: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

paragraphs.text: A new scene that St. John witnessed, his vision of a new angel coming down from heaven. Many interpreters believed that he is a symbol of Christ Himself, and others held that he is merely an angel commissioned by Christ to carry out His will ... and the scene in which the angel appeared shows the great mission he was commissioned to accomplish.

The key of the bottomless pit: a scene that suggests to us that the abyss is a place with doors, but the spiritual meaning intended is that the abyss, although it is the place of Satan and his followers, is under the absolute authority of God, who holds its key.
A great chain in his hand: a chain is used for binding criminals, and the whole scene is an entrance to what is coming.

entries.section: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

paragraphs.text: The chain was used to bind Satan, and let us notice the use of four titles for the name of Satan at his seizure.
The dragon: it is the title of Satan in the Book of Revelation and means the chief of the demons, and among his followers were "the beast and the false prophet."
That old serpent: that is, the one who seduced Adam and Eve in Paradise long ago.
Satan: the most common name, and its meaning is the accuser and the envier of the children of God.

The devil: the enemy of all righteousness and goodness. See also the meanings in (ch. 12:9). The purpose of listing all these names is to confirm that the seizure of Satan has been accomplished and there is no room for doubt, and to bring the picture closer to our minds ... as when the daily newspapers write the news of the arrest of a criminal and mention his four-part name to confirm his identity.

Bound him a thousand years: this "thousand years" has stirred controversy over determining the earthly time of its beginning, and whether it has already happened or is yet to happen ...?! The well-known principle is that Holy Scripture is interpreted in the light of Holy Scripture; and because Christ Himself pointed to the time of the binding of Satan when He said:

"No man can enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man" (Mt 12:29). "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven" (Lk 10:18). "Now shall the prince of this world be cast out" (Jn 12:31). Therefore the Church believes that this binding coincided with the Incarnation of Christ and the dispensation of His saving work on the wood of the Cross, and Satan, who used to bind people in ancient times (Lk 13:16), has become bound by the authority of Christ.

entries.section: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

paragraphs.text: Cast him into the bottomless pit: that is, his kingdom (the abyss) became the place of his imprisonment.
Shut him up: a confirmation of God's authority and of the key that was with the angel.

Set a seal upon him: a pictorial expression meaning inability to come out and that no one is permitted to open for him. That he should deceive the nations no more: that is, the purpose of binding Satan is to give relative rest to the world after the multitude of his evils.

Till the thousand years should be fulfilled: the end of the thousand years is linked to the beginning of the signs of the Second Coming of the Lord Christ, and it was already pointed out that this thousand years is not earthly time.

The meaning intended from the whole verse is that the seizure of Satan has been accomplished by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption of mankind, and his residence in the abyss has also been fixed, and Satan no longer has authority over man as he had, but his present presence in the abyss does not prevent him, even after his binding, from continuing his wars and spreading his thoughts and confusion and seduction. He is like one who barks behind walls, yet his barking still has an effect on many, frightening them and disturbing them and making them fall into various sins, but he no longer has the authority to take the believers to hell, the place of his kingdom, rather they enter the paradise of bliss, the place where the righteous wait, and it has become easy to overcome his wars by the power of Christ and the Cross.
He must be loosed a little season: that is, before the final coming of Christ he will also be permitted to wage his last war before his final judgment.

entries.section: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

paragraphs.text: I saw thrones: that is, great heavenly seats.

They sat upon them: the Lord Christ promised the twelve to sit on thrones around Him in His Kingdom (Mt 19:28). And judgment was given unto them: connected with the same preceding promise, as the Lord Christ gave the Fathers the Apostles the right to pass judgments and judge the nations (Mt 19:28, 29). St. John tells us of two scenes in one picture: the first scene is the sitting of the Apostles and saints on thrones around His throne in the council of His rule, and the second scene concerns all the believers who enjoy being with Christ and accompanying Him in His glory. St. John specified for us that these people are those who did not worship the beast nor his image and did not receive his mark, and all this was discussed and explained before in (ch. 13:15-18), and the meaning intended is that none will reign with Christ except the one who resisted Satan and rejected him and overcame him.

entries.section: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

paragraphs.text: But the rest of the dead: that is, the people who will not share with Christ in His reign and glory because they followed Satan and the mark of the beast and did not repent, and therefore they were described as the dead, that is, dead in God's sight spiritually even if they live on earth in their bodies.

Lived not again until the thousand years were finished: they did not repent and did not enjoy life with Christ in His Church on earth during earthly time, that is, the thousand years in which Christ reigns over the hearts of His children in the Church and those of them who have departed in the paradise of bliss. The meaning is that these wicked, that is, the spiritually dead, have no place in the Church or in Paradise, and this remains throughout the thousand years, that is, the period in which we live now, and the Holy Spirit calls everyone to rise from their death by faith in Christ and by attachment to the Church. This is the first resurrection: what is the meaning of the first resurrection, and what then is the second resurrection, and are there two resurrections of the bodies or what?..!
Because of the importance of this subject and its connection with the faith of the Church, we clarify the following:

1- That there is only one resurrection of the bodies, and that is at the Second Coming of Christ and the end of life on earth and the beginning of the general judgment (Jn 5:28, 29, 2 Thess 1:8-10, 2 Pet 3:9).
2- The meaning of the first resurrection is the spiritual resurrection, which is rising by repentance and Baptism from the death of sin, as Holy Scripture itself confirmed.

"And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; wherein in time past ye walked ... And hath raised us up together in Christ Jesus" (Eph 2:1-6). "Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God" (Col 2:12). "Whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die (rise) forever" (Jn 11:26). "We know that we have passed from death unto life (resurrection)" (1 Jn 3:14). From the foregoing the meaning of the first resurrection can be confirmed .. it is faith in the Lord Christ, rejection of Satan and resistance to him, receiving Baptism from the holy Church, and perseverance and striving to the last breath. As for the second resurrection, as we mentioned, it is the resurrection of the bodies on the day of judgment and entrance into the eternal Kingdom.

entries.section: (1) The seizing of Satan and the thousand-year reign

paragraphs.text: For this reason the one who had a part in the first resurrection deserved blessing and praise, "that is, the true, steadfast believers" who died to the desires of the world, so they rose and lived in the world with the mind of resurrection and victory.
The second death: the expression the second death can be understood in more than one way.
First: if the temporal death of the body is considered the first death, then the second death becomes an expression that signifies the eternal perdition of man.
Second: if the first death is considered the life of sin before repentance, then the second death becomes the temporal death of the body.

The meaning in either case is that whoever has the first resurrection in Christ by faith, Baptism and repentance will not be harmed at all by the temporal death of his body, as the Lord Christ said, "Fear not them which kill the body," since they have no authority over the spirit. For the spirit moves to Paradise and rejoices there and is not affected by the death of the body on earth, then it is immortal afterward in the eternal Kingdom after the Second Coming of Christ. On such the second death hath no power: a parenthetical sentence confirming that they will rise on the last day and reign forever with Christ. He means that the believers who will live by faith and repentance on earth will be priests of God on earth by the sacrifice of their souls.

They shall be priests of God and of Christ: another reason for their blessing and praise is that they were priests during their lives on earth by offering themselves and their will as a living daily sacrifice before God in their worship and service to Him, and they will also reign by their meekness and Christian conduct over the hearts of those who live with them (Mt 5:5) until the Second Coming of Christ, and the word thousand years here is symbolic, as we explained before that it includes the time from the Incarnation and redemption of Christ until near His Second Coming.

Beloved, be strong and take courage and remain firm in your first resurrection, and remember the promise of the Lord Christ that if you remain, the second death will not harm you and your soul will not perish. But to remain in this resurrection you must avoid all causes of spiritual death ... so flee from the enticements of the world and its desires and hold fast to your daily repentance, for repentance is your resurrection, and if you leave it, the second death will not leave you.
A review of our doctrine of the thousand years and the millennial reign of Christ:

While some (from other denominations) have gone in interpretation to say that the thousand years is a thousand literal years in which Christ will reign on earth and manage His affairs with His saints from Jerusalem, our Church rejects this teaching altogether for more than one reason:
1- Christ Himself declared more than once that His kingdom is not of this world.
2- Christ's announcement of His coming a second and final time, and this time witnesses the dissolution of nature and the falling of the planets and the end of life on earth (Mt 24).
3- All the times and events in the Book of Revelation are symbolic events with spiritual meanings.. so why do we understand this particular time literally?.!

entries.section: (2) Satan loosed for a little while

paragraphs.text: When the thousand years are expired: that is, near the end of earthly life and shortly before the Second Coming of the Lord Christ, and for a short period.

Shall be loosed out of his prison: that is, God permits him for a short period to use all his power and violence, and it will be a hard period in which he tries to lead the elect astray, but the power of God supports them so that they do not stumble.

entries.section: (2) Satan loosed for a little while

paragraphs.text: These two verses make clear to us the last battle, which was mentioned without elaboration or detail.. and it can be described as follows:
1- Satan goes out to gather his supporters for war from every corner of the world, "the four quarters of the earth."

2- Their number was beyond counting and they surrounded the Church in a fierce war, for they came from the breadth of the earth with their evil to destroy the Church, "the camp of the saints and the beloved city."
3- The end was swift and terrifying, for God sent down divine fire from heaven (the bowl of His wrath: ch. 16), and it devoured them all.

Gog and Magog: a figure for Satan and his helpers, but originally they were two kings of the northern kingdoms that fought and were hostile to Israel in ancient times, and about whom Ezekiel prophesied (Ezek 38:2) and about their severe destruction (Ezek 38:

entries.section: (2) Satan loosed for a little while

paragraphs.text: As for their supreme commander and the manager of the whole kingdom of evil, who deceived and led many astray after him, his fate was eternal perdition in the lake of fire and brimstone, and his two companions also, his greatest helpers in the kingdom of evil, the beast and the false prophet.

As for their fate, it is final and eternal torment without ceasing or mercy, "day and night." And this is a declaration to us all that God's justice and vengeance on the wicked is coming .. coming however long He is patient with them. It is noted, dear reader, that after the end of this scene Satan and his helpers are not mentioned again.

The lake of fire and brimstone: it is the eternal place prepared for the torment of the wicked, and it is not hell and not the abyss either .. none of the wicked will enter this place before the coming of Christ and His judgment.

If many oppose you in your righteous conduct, do not be disturbed, and if they press you, whether those close to you or those in authority over you, to sin against God, do not agree with them, but obey the commandments of God before any man. Persevere in your striving, knowing that all evil will pass away and God will reward you in the end for your faithfulness, and will also support you in your confrontation with the world until you complete the days of your sojourn in peace.

And I saw: with this expression St. John moves us to the scene of the general and final judgment.. A great white throne: that is, the throne of Christ Himself, and he called it great to distinguish it from any other throne, such as the thrones of the disciples or the saints (v. 4). And whiteness signifies absolute purity and cleanness, which God alone possesses.
The earth and the heaven fled away: they passed away and had no place or life, and heaven here means the heaven of the stars and planets.

The scene here is frightening and awesome, as Christ Himself sat on His throne of judgment, pure and holy and just, after all the signs of the material world known to us had passed away, and we had entered the time of endless eternity.
All the dead appeared before the throne, risen in their new bodies, from the greatest of them to the smallest, for the resurrection is for all, even for children.
The books were opened: that is, the books that contained and recorded the works of each one of them were opened.
The book of life: another book was opened in which were written the names of the heirs of eternal life.
The dead were judged: each one was called to account for all the works he did in his life, which were written in the books, since everything was recorded.
According to their works: that is, not according to their positions or great duties on earth but according to their works, in agreement with or contrary to the commandments of Christ.

St. John describes how the judgment is carried out, for on the day of judgment each person is confronted with all his works that he did consciously and knowingly, whether small or great, for everything that man did not repent of is recorded against him and kept, and he cannot deny it or justify it.
The sea gave up the dead: the direct meaning is that whoever died by drowning in the sea and was not buried rose also.
Death and hell: that is, whoever was dead and held in hell rose also from death for judgment.

The general meaning of this verse is that since God alone is the One who has authority over all creation and commanded the beginning of the judgment, all the bodies rose regardless of where they were or where they were buried and were united with the spirits so that the judgment may be carried out according to God's just decree and He gives each one according to his work. This verse comes depicting the sea and the abyss as persons, guards who were entrusted with the spirits and bodies, and now the time has come for their handing them over for judgment.

Because death and hell are bound up with sin, they became enemies of God, as St. Paul said, "The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death" (1 Cor 15:26), and because after the resurrection there will be no other death and no need of the abyss (the place where the wicked or Satan wait), God cast them also into the lake, which is the lake of eternal torment mentioned in (v. 10). This is the second death: that is, this is the death and eternal perdition after which there is no life or resurrection, and it is the perpetual torment in the lake of fire and brimstone, and it is extremely horrible.

That is, whoever had no good life or constant repentance and by his evil works refused to have his name written in the book of the eternal inheritance (the book of life) became rejected and was cast into the lake, just as the dragon, the beast and the false prophet and all the followers of evil, and death and hell, were cast, for the fate is one for all the wicked.

My beloved God, the scene of judgment is a very terrifying scene, at which the soul trembles and fears, so keep it present before me always, my God, that I may not be negligent nor turn aside to a life of evil, and make me always pray with Your Church the Prayer of the Veil (from the Agpeya), saying: "Your judgment is fearful, when men are gathered and the angels stand. The books are opened, the deeds are revealed and the thoughts are examined. What judgment will be mine, who am convicted by my sins; who will quench my darkness if You do not have mercy on me, O Lord? For You are compassionate toward mankind.

The new heaven and the new earth: introduction to the chapter: after Satan and his helpers and all the wicked are cast into the lake burning with fire and brimstone, and the scene of judgment, the Spirit moves us to a wonderful scene, which is His speaking about the Kingdom of Heaven and the meeting of Christ with His holy children.

entries.section: (1) The dwelling of God with men

paragraphs.text: A new heaven and a new earth: that is, a vision of a new creation that men have not known before and that has not even entered our imagination.

It is noted that at the beginning of the Holy Bible (Gen 1) the discussion was about the creation of heaven and earth, and as the Holy Bible ends, the discussion is also about "a new heaven and a new earth," and to confirm this new picture of heaven and earth, he adds for us and affirms the passing away of the material earth and the heaven of stars on which and under which men were accustomed to live.

As for the reason for the existence of a new heaven and a new earth, it is a figure for a new life that has no relation to the laws of the old life, and perhaps the most important of its features is the constant presence of God in it, as we will understand from the following verses, so it is the spiritual heaven and earth, which befit the presence of God.

And there was no more sea: the sea points to division and disturbance, for it is what divided the dry land, and its high waves are a symbol of turmoil, agitation and lack of peace.. and the meaning intended is that in the Kingdom there is nothing of human conflicts or division.

entries.section: (1) The dwelling of God with men

paragraphs.text: I John: to confirm what is coming .. as when a person says, "I saw with my own eyes."
New Jerusalem: a symbol of the Kingdom of Heaven.

St. John continues his vision and declares to us that he saw the holy city of God, given as a gift by God (coming down from heaven), for the victors to inherit and enjoy; and to describe the intensity of its beauty, St. John found no more eloquent expression than that it is "a bride adorned for her husband," because it is known among people that the most splendid picture of a young woman is on the day of her wedding.

entries.section: (1) The dwelling of God with men

paragraphs.text: And in joy and gladness the heavenly creation announces, "a great voice out of heaven," that the most beautiful name for this great city is that it is "the tabernacle of God with men," that is, the place where God will bring together with men in permanent dwelling, where we all see Him "face to face" (1 Cor 13:12), and all will be the people and flock of God, while God is in the midst of all in the glory of His divinity, the source of eternal satisfaction and happiness.

"The tabernacle of God with men": the divine inspiration used the word "tabernacle" in describing the first church that God made in its finest details, which is the "tabernacle of meeting," because God wanted to declare to His people that He wants to dwell in their midst also, since the tent, the "tabernacle," was pitched in the midst of the tribes of the people of the children of Israel. And the Church also, "the tabernacle," is a permanent symbol of heaven, where man meets God in it, and the tabernacle of God with men is also a statement of the greatness of His love for the human race, for this is the pleasure of His heart, to be like a father among his children, and also a statement of His humility and condescension.

entries.section: (1) The dwelling of God with men

paragraphs.text: God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes: of course there will be no tears at all in the New Jerusalem, but it is enough for us to contemplate this beautiful scene that St. John portrayed for us, for Christ in the perfection of His tenderness stretches His hand over the face of each of us to wipe from our mind every memory of pain or weariness or distress that man passed through during his first life and his striving for the sake of God's name. And the scene, besides highlighting the tenderness of Christ, also shows how much God feels for us and does not forget the faithfulness of His children, and finally God confirms to us the idea of compensation with rest and happiness for the former pain; how wonderful is Your tenderness, my God, and the gentleness of Your feelings and Your justice and Your love for Your flock, O Good Shepherd.
The former things are passed away: a confirmation that the time of sorrows, pains and crying are all former things that have no place where there is endless happiness in the presence of God.

entries.section: (1) The dwelling of God with men

paragraphs.text: A direct command came from the Lord Christ, "him that sat upon the throne," to John to write His true and faithful words and promises, and they are words that confirm what was already indicated in the previous four verses, of the passing away of the old things and God's bringing of new things that we did not know before .. but they are the source of our eternal happiness.

entries.section: (1) The dwelling of God with men

paragraphs.text: It is done: this saying is Christ's, and its meaning is that He has already accomplished this new creation and prepared His Kingdom to receive His believing children after the judgment; and Christ used this expression twice, the first when He poured out His wrath on the wicked (16:17) and the second here when He glorified His children in the Kingdom. And the expression "It is done" reminds us also of our Savior's saying on the wood of the Cross, "It is finished" (Jn 19:30), and He means the completion of the redemption, which we receive in perfection in eternity.

Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end: an expression that Christ used in describing Himself in (ch. 1:8) at the beginning of the Book of Revelation, and it is an expression that concerns His divinity, for He is the source of all things and their Creator, and He is also the eternal, everlasting God.

I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely: these words remind us of the conversation of the Lord Jesus with the Samaritan woman "Jn 4," which she did not understand at first ... and the spiritual meaning here is that for all who thirst for righteousness and holiness (the water of life), Christ is the only source of their supply, whether this is during earthly time or in the time of absolute eternity ...
